agent_findings_by_dimension.dimension: INGESTION ROOT CAUSE — why WebSearch result ingestion produced 3 wrong winners on 2026-08-08
agent_findings_by_dimension.summary: Not one failure mode but three, stacked on a channel with zero mechanical validation. (a) ADJACENT-DAY ECHO is proven for two games: DET@SF was ingested as 2-5 and TB@SEA as 2-1 for 8/8 — byte-for-byte the 8/7 finals already on file (truth: DET 8-0, TB 3-2). (b) ORIENTATION FLIP is proven for ATH@BOS: ingested away 3 / home 7, truth away 7 / home 3 — same digits, reversed sides, with home_win=1 and margin=+4 derived from the flipped pair so the row is internally consistent. (c) ANCHORED FABRICATION for LAA@MIA: 4-3 matches no real game on any date — the away score is the 8/7 value (4) and the home score is the 8/7 value +1 (2→3); truth was 0-7. Underneath all three: (d) no cross-source verification is even recorded — unlike every prior day since 7/29, the 8/8 ingest wrote NO evidence file at all (commit 6e436db touched only results.csv, the grading JSON, ml_asof and a WNBA evidence file), so provenance for graded numbers is a single free-text CSV cell reading "websearch_multi_source(ESPN/MLB.com) 2026-08-09" with no per-game URL or source id; and (e) no structural gate exists anywhere — healthcheck.py's results.csv block checks row count, duplicate game_ids, home_win/total non-null and freshness, none of which can detect a wrong score. The 8/5 "echo guard" did not prevent this because it was never a control: it is a prose string in a data file and a paragraph in progress.md, executed only by the model remembering to re-search. Grep for "echo" across harness/ returns zero code. Worse, the same adjacent-day snippet-bleed had already fired that same day in the injury layer and been written up (2026-08-08_slate_corrections.json: "The snippet conflated his 8/7 return with today") nine hours before it recurred in results. On confidence: there is NO confidence-to-write gate. The vocabulary exists (data/feeds/MANIFEST.json: "HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW — LOW/unsourced items are flagged, never fed to a model") but it binds only the feeds layer; results.csv has no confidence or tier column, the evidence/websearch/*_finals.json schema has no confidence field at all, and harness/build_ml_asof.py consumes every row with status=final regardless of source. The prior session labelled the entire WebSearch channel MEDIUM ("treat every status as 'expected,' not 'confirmed'") and then used that same channel to write finals that were graded as authoritative.

findings.title: Verbatim prior-day echo: DET@SF and TB@SEA ingested as exact copies of the 8/7 finals
findings.evidence: /home/user/sports-model/data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv at commit 6e436db — row `mlb:2026:ws0808-DETSF,2026-08-08,final,DET,SF,2,5` vs 8/7 row `mlb:2026:ws0807-DETSF,2026-08-07,final,DET,SF,2,5`; row `mlb:2026:ws0808-TBSEA,2026-08-08,final,TB,SEA,2,1` vs 8/7 row `mlb:2026:823103,2026-08-07,final,TB,SEA,2,1`. Corroborated by /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-07_finals.json, whose source_notes for those games are date-bearing page ids the 8/8 search would re-hit: DET@SF = 'espn recap 401816435 + b-ref SFN202608070 + CBS DET@SF (SF 5-2 Oracle)' (SFN2026080-7-0 encodes 8/7); TB@SEA = 'mlb gameday 823103 (TB 2-1)'. Authoritative: DET 8-0, TB 3-2 (/home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/2026-08-10_results_correction.json).
findings.impact: Two of the four bad rows, including one wrong winner (SF credited over DET), are the previous night's game re-recorded under today's date. Both teams are in a series, so the search layer returns the prior recap for an identical query; nothing in the pipeline compares today's row to yesterday's.
findings.recommendation: Add a mechanical duplicate-score check to harness/healthcheck.py: for every consecutive-day same-matchup pair, FAIL if (away_score, home_score) is identical. Measured alarm rate on the full 2026 file at commit 6e436db is 22 of 1127 pairs = 1.95% (19 of them genuine statsapi-era repeats), i.e. roughly one alarm every six slates — and it fires on BOTH DET@SF and TB@SEA. Each alarm requires only a dedicated recap re-check before the row may be written, exactly the procedure the 8/5 note described but never enforced.

findings.title: No structural validation gate on ingested results — healthcheck cannot detect a wrong score
findings.evidence: /home/user/sports-model/harness/healthcheck.py lines 29-42: the entire results.csv integrity block checks only `len(finals)>=1505`, `no duplicate game_ids`, `home_win in (0,1) and total != ''`, and staleness `days_stale<=2`. All four passed on the 8/8 ingest. Synthetic keys ws0807-DETSF and ws0808-DETSF are distinct strings, so the duplicate-id check cannot see a repeated game either.
findings.impact: The repo carries an unusually strong control surface (hash-chained forecast registry with a falsification battery, lineage verifiers A and B, ml_asof byte-identical rebuild, computed gate counter) — all of it validates provenance of MODEL identity and arithmetic, and none of it validates the CONTENT of an outcome. A 27%-wrong slate passed HEALTHY.
findings.recommendation: Extend the healthcheck results block with content checks that are cheap and falsifiable: (1) consecutive-day duplicate score; (2) linescore-sum reconciliation where the source provides innings (already implemented in harness/parse_box_dump.py — wire it into the gate); (3) every date with rows in results.csv must have a matching evidence file on disk, and every ingested row's `source` must name it; (4) refuse ingestion of any date where a game on the frozen slate .psv has no result row (the 7/23 missing-game class).

findings.title: No evidence artifact was written for 8/8 at all — cross-source verification is unrecorded and unfalsifiable
findings.evidence: `git show --name-only 6e436db` lists exactly: data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv, data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading.json, data/mlb/ml_asof/{dataset.jsonl,exclusions.json,manifest.json}, data/wnba/evidence_2026-08-08_finals.json. /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/websearch/ contains files for 7/29-7/31, 8/1-8/2, 8/3, 8/4, 8/5, 8/6, 8/7 — and nothing for 8/8. The only surviving provenance is the CSV `source` cell 'websearch_multi_source(ESPN/MLB.com) 2026-08-09', with no per-game source_note, URL or page id, versus 8/7 where every game carried one.
findings.impact: The claim 'multi_source' is unverifiable and, given three wrong rows, almost certainly false for those games. Because no page ids were recorded, the very signal that would have exposed the echo — the 8/8 search returning the same b-ref/ESPN ids already logged for 8/7 — was thrown away. This is the (d) failure: cross-source verification did not merely fail, it left no trace that it was attempted.
findings.recommendation: Make the evidence file a precondition, not a byproduct: no row may be appended to results.csv unless data/mlb/evidence/<DATE>_finals.json exists, contains a per-game record with at least two distinct source identifiers, and the ingest writes the evidence file's sha256 into the row's source column. Reject any evidence record whose source ids appear in the prior day's evidence file for the same matchup — that single rule is the mechanised echo guard.

findings.title: ATH@BOS is an away/home orientation flip that no consistency check can catch, because the derived fields were computed from the flipped pair
findings.evidence: /home/user/sports-model/data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv at 6e436db: `mlb:2026:824726,2026-08-08,final,ATH,BOS,3,7,1,4,10` — away 3, home 7, home_win 1, margin +4. Authoritative is ATH 7, BOS 3 (/home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/2026-08-10_results_correction.json, linescore_verified true). Same two digits, opposite sides. Not an echo: 8/7 ATH@BOS was 1-13 (/home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-07_finals.json).
findings.impact: home_win, margin and total were all derived from the flipped pair, so the row is perfectly self-consistent and reconciles against itself, the total, and the ml_asof rebuild. Orientation errors are invisible to every internal check the repo has. This flip also handed the night's biggest market favourite (BOS, mkt_home_prob 0.702 in cards/2026-08-08_card.json) a win it did not get.
findings.recommendation: Require the ingest to record the WINNER'S TEAM NAME as a separate string field taken verbatim from the source, then assert that the team named as winner equals the team with the higher recorded score. A headline reading 'Athletics 7, Red Sox 3' cannot then be written as away 3 / home 7. Pair this with the linescore-sum check in harness/parse_box_dump.py, which independently binds each score to its own team's innings.

findings.title: LAA@MIA 4-3 corresponds to no real game on any date — an anchored reconstruction, not a transcription
findings.evidence: Ingested `mlb:2026:ws0808-LAAMIA,2026-08-08,final,LAA,MIA,4,3`. The 8/7 game was LAA 4-2 (/home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-07_finals.json, source_note 'foxsports boxscore 96406 (LAA 4-2)' — note: single source, no gamePk). Authoritative 8/8 is MIA 7-0. The ingested pair keeps the 8/7 away score exactly (4) and moves the home score by one (2→3).
findings.impact: This is the (c) failure mode and the most dangerous of the four, because it defeats every content check that compares against a real record: it is not a duplicate of yesterday, so a duplicate-score alarm misses it, and it is internally consistent, so arithmetic checks miss it. It flipped a game the market had at MIA 59.4% into a 'winning dog' — one of the three legs of the 'compression caught winning dogs' conclusion in data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading.json.
findings.recommendation: Only a tier-1 record with an internal cross-check can catch this class. Adopt the tier discipline already drafted in harness/parse_box_dump.py's docstring and make it binding: tier 3 (search snippet/aggregator) may write a row only with status='provisional', and a provisional row may never be used to grade, to append to grades.jsonl, or to enter data/mlb/ml_asof. Finalisation requires tier 1 with a linescore that sums.

findings.title: There is no confidence-to-write gate: results.csv has no confidence or tier column and the finals evidence schema has no confidence field
findings.evidence: /home/user/sports-model/data/feeds/MANIFEST.json defines `confidence: HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW — LOW/unsourced items are flagged, never fed to a model`, but its scope is `schema_per_pull` for data/feeds only. results.csv header (/home/user/sports-model/data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv line 1) has 21 columns and no confidence or tier field. The evidence/websearch/*_finals.json schema is (record_id, retrieved_utc, provenance_class, supersede_rule, games) — no confidence key on any day. /home/user/sports-model/data/feeds/2026-08-08_reconciliation.json data_quality_flags: 'Whole dataset is search-snippet level (all game blocks MEDIUM confidence) ... Treat every status as "expected," not "confirmed"'. harness/build_ml_asof.py consumes every status=final row with no provenance filter ('every final in results.csv appears either as a dataset row or in the exclusion records'). RESULT_SOURCE_TIER is named only in harness/parse_box_dump.py's docstring; it is not a column anywhere.
findings.impact: The system can express confidence but cannot act on it. The same MEDIUM-confidence channel the prior session explicitly distrusted for injuries wrote finals that were treated as authoritative by the grader, by build_ml_asof (15 contaminated rows appended and a new vintage hash cut, commit 6e436db), and by every downstream consumer. There is literally no code path where a confidence value can block a write.
findings.recommendation: Add `source_tier` (1|2|3) and `status` in {provisional, final} as real columns on results.csv, backfill them from the existing source strings, and enforce in healthcheck: (a) any graded game must be tier 1; (b) build_ml_asof excludes non-final rows into the exclusion record rather than the dataset; (c) forecast_registry.append_grade refuses a grade whose referenced result row is provisional. Also add `confidence` to the finals evidence schema so the value exists at the point of capture, not only in the feeds sidecar.

findings.title: The 8/5 'echo guard' was never a control — it is prose in a data file, executed only by the model remembering
findings.evidence: The guard exists in exactly two places, both narrative: /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-05_finals.json key `echo_guard` ('three first-pass scores were 8/4-echoes and were CORRECTED by dedicated recap searches before recording...'), and /home/user/sports-model/docs/progress.md line 1427. A grep for 'echo' across harness/ and engine/ returns no code — only those prose strings plus a one-line note in data/mlb/slates/2026-08-09_prep.json. /home/user/sports-model/docs/OPERATING_WORKFLOW.md step 5 says only 'Postgame — ingest the official result', with no definition of 'official', no evidence requirement and no cross-day check.
findings.impact: The guard's success on 8/5 (and the analogous extra-innings re-check on 8/7) created the appearance of a hardened process while the actual defence remained one agent's vigilance in one session. On 8/8 the vigilance was not applied and nothing else existed. This is the general pattern in this repo's failures: lessons are written to sidecar JSON and progress.md, where the next session may or may not read them, instead of to healthcheck.py, where they execute unconditionally.
findings.recommendation: Treat every ingestion lesson as owing a healthcheck assertion. Convert the three existing prose lessons now: echo (8/5) → consecutive-day duplicate check; extra-innings regulation-score error (7/29) → require an innings count or linescore for any game whose recorded total differs from a second source; missing game (7/23) → slate-completeness reconciliation against the frozen .psv. Add a standing rule to AGENTS.md that a correction sidecar is not closed until its check is in the gate.

findings.title: The identical failure mode fired nine hours earlier the same day, in the injury layer, and was documented rather than fixed
findings.evidence: /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_slate_corrections.json (built_utc 2026-08-08T22:30:22Z): item 'Jose Ramirez NOT in Cleveland's posted 8/8 lineup' — was: 'WebSearch snippet said "Ramirez back" -> I stated "confirmed back for 8/8"'; now: 'He played 8/7; the OFFICIAL 8/8 lineup is Kwan, Adell, ... (no Ramirez). The snippet conflated his 8/7 return with today.' The 8/8 results ingest ran at 2026-08-09T05:42:19Z (ingested_utc in results.csv), roughly seven hours later, and made the same adjacent-day conflation on three games.
findings.impact: The prior session had already named the mechanism precisely — search snippets attributing yesterday's event to today — and had it in front of it as a written correction. It still shipped the same error in a higher-stakes field. This is strong evidence the failure is systemic to snippet ingestion rather than incidental, and that narrative self-correction does not transfer across tasks within a session, let alone across sessions.
findings.recommendation: Generalise the rule beyond scores: any WebSearch-derived fact asserted 'as of DATE' must carry the source's own date string, and the ingest must refuse a fact whose source date is not DATE. Applies identically to lineups, probables, injuries and finals. This is a single shared validator, not four.

findings.title: The discriminating signal was present in the data and never used: all three echo/fabrication games were in the unresolved-gamePk cohort
findings.evidence: Of the 15 rows for 2026-08-08 at commit 6e436db, 7 carry numeric gamePks and 8 carry synthetic keys (ws0808-LAAMIA, -NYMPIT, -CHCKC, -COLSTL, -BALTEX, -HOUSD, -DETSF, -TBSEA). The three echo/fabrication errors (LAA@MIA, DET@SF, TB@SEA) are all in the synthetic cohort: 3 of 8 wrong = 37.5%, versus 1 of 7 = 14.3% for the gamePk-resolved cohort (the ATH@BOS orientation flip). DET@SF and LAA@MIA also had no gamePk on 8/7 — the same two games failed to resolve two days running.
findings.impact: An unresolved gamePk is a direct proxy for 'no authoritative gameday page was actually opened for this game'. The prior session recorded that fact in the primary key of every affected row and then treated all 15 rows as equally authoritative when grading. The 8/8 slate .psv (/home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/slates/2026-08-08_slate.psv) carries no gamePks either, so there was no reference list to resolve against.
findings.recommendation: Make gamePk resolution a hard precondition for a final row: no gamePk, no finalised result — the row is written provisional and excluded from grading and from ml_asof until resolved. Separately, pull and freeze the day's gamePk list from the schedule at slate-freeze time (the OPERATING_WORKFLOW T-120 step already says 're-pull gamePk'), so postgame ingestion joins against a known key set rather than inventing ws-prefixed keys. Note also that the 8/8 numeric gamePks cannot be audited at all, since no evidence file records where they came from.

findings.title: The 8/8 grading bypassed the hash-chained forecast/grade registry entirely, so the repo's strongest governance machinery never saw the numbers reported to the owner
findings.evidence: /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/forecasts/head.json: 71 forecasts, 69 grades; the last rows in forecasts.jsonl and grades.jsonl are all slate_date 2026-08-04 (P4-20260804-*). Commit 6e436db added no rows to either file. The reported figures (V13 7/15, market 6/15, Pass-1 7/12, attractive plays 3/3) exist only in the free-form /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading.json, with no forecast_id linkage, no chain entry and no evidence reference. harness/forecast_registry.py validate_records applies only one rule to grades — 'no matching forecast' — and never validates the free-text `source` field, so even a registered grade need not point at an evidence file that exists.
findings.impact: forecast_registry.verify() passed and healthcheck reported HEALTHY, because the registry only checks internal consistency of what is in it; there is no completeness rule requiring that a graded slate reported to the owner be registered. The registry's falsification battery, hash chain and R6 supersession machinery — the exact tools used correctly for the 7/29 correction (G2-* superseding rows) — were unavailable for the 8/8 numbers because those numbers were never enrolled.
findings.recommendation: Require that any grading result communicated to the owner be a registry read, not a hand-written JSON: healthcheck should FAIL when a data/mlb/forecasts/<DATE>_grading.json exists with no corresponding grade rows for that date. Strengthen grade validation to require `source` to name an evidence file that exists on disk and whose sha256 matches, mirroring the `original_file_hash` rule already enforced on forecasts.

findings.title: Contamination propagated forward: 15 bad rows entered the ml_asof dataset and the 8/9 card was built on distorted team form
findings.evidence: Commit 6e436db appended 15 rows to data/mlb/ml_asof/dataset.jsonl and rewrote manifest.json (new vintage hash). /home/user/sports-model/harness/daily_card.py lines 28-36 build season RF/RA from every row in results.csv with `if r['status']!='final' or r['total']=='': continue` and no provenance filter. Commit c3df775 ('Prep 8/9: slate frozen + preliminary card') was cut after the bad ingest. Run-level distortion at the time the 8/9 card was built: DET/SF ±5-6 runs each, ATH/BOS ±4, LAA/MIA ±4, TB/SEA ±1 — eight teams' season aggregates.
findings.impact: A results error is not contained to grading; it silently becomes a model input. cards/2026-08-09_card.json contains V13 probabilities for ATH@BOS and other affected teams computed from corrupt RF/RA. The ml_asof vintage hash certifies byte-reproducibility of a contaminated dataset — determinism was preserved, correctness was not.
findings.recommendation: Once source_tier exists, exclude provisional rows from both daily_card team-form accumulation and build_ml_asof eligibility. Separately, when a result is corrected, healthcheck should FAIL until every downstream artifact whose build date postdates the bad row has been rebuilt or explicitly marked superseded — currently nothing links a corrected result to the cards and datasets it poisoned.

findings.title: The errors were not neutral noise — they bent the slate toward the narrative the grading file then reported
findings.evidence: cards/2026-08-08_card.json market probabilities vs what was ingested: LAA@MIA mkt_home_prob 0.594 (MIA) — ingested as an LAA win, truth MIA 7-0; DET@SF mkt_home_prob 0.472 (DET favoured) — ingested as an SF win, truth DET 8-0; ATH@BOS mkt_home_prob 0.702 (BOS) — ingested as a BOS win, truth ATH 7-3. data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading.json then reported night_context 'UPSET-HEAVY: market favorites went 6/15 (40%)' and concluded 'compression toward .500 caught winning dogs'. Two of the three flips manufactured upsets; correcting all three moves the market-favourite count to 7/15.
findings.impact: The three fabricated/echoed results happened to produce a more dramatic and more internally coherent story than the truth, and that story became the reported lesson. With n=3 this is an observation rather than a demonstrated bias, but it is the characteristic signature of reconstruction-from-prior rather than random transcription error, and it means snippet ingestion should be treated as capable of confirming whatever narrative the session is already forming.
findings.recommendation: Enforce read/grade separation in time and role: the agent that ingests results must not hold the card's probabilities or the night's narrative in context. The OPERATING_WORKFLOW already separates Pregame and Validation agents — extend it so postgame ingestion is a third, model-blind step (or, better, a parser with no model in the loop, as harness/parse_box_dump.py now is) whose output is frozen before any grading reads it.

findings.title: Remediation-side: the 8/10 correction mutated the archived 8/8 rows in place rather than appending superseding rows
findings.evidence: Current /home/user/sports-model/data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv rows 1757, 1758, 1768, 1770 now read the corrected scores with source 'CORRECTED_2026-08-10 owner_box_dump(tier1) sha256:5e978c3c83405d03 parse_box_dump.py' while retaining the ORIGINAL ingested_utc 2026-08-09T05:42:19Z. Contrast the 7/29 grade correction, which appended superseding G2-* rows and preserved the originals (data/mlb/forecasts/grades.jsonl, 'superseding grade appended, original preserved (R6)').
findings.impact: results.csv alone no longer shows what was ingested on 8/9; the ingested_utc is now attached to values that were not ingested at that time. The audit trail survives only in git and in data/mlb/evidence/2026-08-10_results_correction.json. Under R6 (append-only, errors logged not erased), a row that was used to grade and to build a dataset is an archived record.
findings.recommendation: Append superseding rows keyed as corrections (with supersedes_game_id and a fresh ingested_utc) and mark the originals superseded, matching the grades.jsonl pattern; or, if in-place is deliberate for a join-key-stable CSV, record the original values in the row itself so results.csv remains self-describing. Also note RESULT_SOURCE_TIER is referenced in harness/parse_box_dump.py's docstring but does not yet exist as a column — the tier discipline is currently documented, not enforced.

agent_findings_by_dimension.dimension: Downstream impact of bad 8/8 result data
agent_findings_by_dimension.summary:
I rebuilt the 8/8 grading from first principles off the frozen card (/home/user/sports-model/cards/2026-08-08_card.json) and the moneylines in data/mlb/odds/2026-08-08_gameboards.json. My reproduction of the prior session's numbers using the BAD results is exact on every metric (V13 7/15, Brier 0.2558, market 6/15, home 10/15, Pass-1 7/12, raw-V13 evening 6/12, attractive 3/3), which validates the methodology. Recomputing with the authoritative results gives: V13 8/15 (was 7/15), Brier 0.2614 (was 0.2558 — WORSE), market favorites 7/15 (was 6/15), home 9/15 (was 10/15), Pass-1 8/12 (was 7/12), raw-V13 evening 7/12 (was 6/12), attractive plays 3/3 UNCHANGED. NOTE: while I was auditing, a concurrent session committed the correction (de87ba3, 04:47Z) with exactly these numbers; my independent recompute confirms every one of them, and results.csv + ml_asof labels are now fixed at HEAD.

CONTAMINATION SCOPE, traced to ground: (1) results.csv — 4 rows, now corrected. (2) ml_asof dataset.jsonl — 4 rows' labels (3x label_home_win, 3x label_margin, 2x label_total), now corrected, and MATERIALITY WAS ZERO for modeling because all 8/8 rows carry eligible_for_evaluation=false; I verified 0 of the 1345 eligible rows are WebSearch-sourced and the latest eligible slate_date is 2026-07-19, so P2 baselines, the P3 sealed holdout, the HFA A1 test and the exposure report are all untouched. (3) Forecast registry — NOT contaminated: forecasts.jsonl contains zero 8/8 rows (71 forecasts, 7/27–8/4 only), grades.jsonl 69 grades, chain intact. (4) state.json — contains no 8/8-derived numbers. (5) Team-form aggregates — the one real propagation path: harness/daily_card.py:28 recomputes season RF/RA from every final in results.csv with no date filter, so the 4 bad rows shifted 8 teams' season rates by up to 7.6%. Exactly one artifact consumed that: cards/2026-08-09_card.json. I rebuilt it both ways in a scratchpad mirror; my reverted build reproduces the committed card bit-for-bit on all 15 home_wp values, so the counterfactual is trustworthy — impact is max |delta home_wp| 0.006, zero side-pick flips, and the 8/9 grading is 11/15 either way with Brier 0.2353 -> 0.2350. The 8/9 conclusion is safe.

CONCLUSIONS: "attractive plays 3/3" and "the disciplined selections cashed" fully SURVIVE (MIL 4-3, CWS 6-3, TB 3-2 all genuinely won). The PASS/$0 decision is unaffected — pre-game, no money. "Upset-heavy, market favorites 6/15 (40%)" WEAKENS to 7/15 (47%). "V13 edged the market" survives at 8/15 vs 7/15, same +1 margin. The injury-overlay "net positive" survives at 8/12 vs 7/12, same +1 delta and same per-game attributions. The claim that materially breaks is the CALIBRATION story: accuracy rose but Brier worsened by +0.0056 because V13's single highest-conviction call of the slate (BOS 0.614) was a loss, while both games it newly gets right were near-coin-flips (0.526, 0.454). The remaining risk is not 8/8 at all — it is the 115 other tier-3 rows and the 56 of 69 registry grades that came from the same pipeline that just measured at 27% wrong.

findings.title: 115 unverified tier-3 WebSearch results remain in results.csv, and 81% of the forecast registry's grades were produced by the same pipeline that just measured 27% wrong
findings.evidence: /home/user/sports-model/data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv still carries 126 finals with `websearch_multi_source` provenance spanning 2026-07-23..2026-08-08 (7/23 x1, 7/29 x16, 7/31 x15, 8/1 x15, 8/2 x15, 8/3 x8, 8/4 x15, 8/5 x15, 8/7 x15, 8/8 x11 — 8/8's other 4 are now tier-1). /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/forecasts/grades.jsonl: 56 of 69 grades cite a websearch source, only 13 cite savant. The measured error rate of that pipeline on the one day now checked against tier-1 is 4/15 games (27%) with 3/15 winner-flips (20%); 7/29 and 7/23 are two further separately-confirmed failures of the same path.
findings.impact: The cumulative diagnostic evidence the promotion gate is accruing rests almost entirely on unverified labels: docs/progress.md:1475 'Cumulative candidate ML: n=54 Brier 0.2543, home 29/54' and docs/progress.md:1473 '31-game cohort: candidate Brier 0.2577 (12/31), market 0.2547 (16/31), paired dBrier +0.00304, t-CI [-0.0158,+0.0218]'. At the observed 20% winner-flip rate, roughly 11 of those 54 outcome labels could be reversed — an order of magnitude larger than the effect sizes those cohorts are measuring, and enough to move the paired dBrier well outside its own CI. The correction commit fixed 8/8 and stopped; it neither re-verified nor flagged the other 115 rows.
findings.recommendation: Treat every tier-3 row as unverified until re-sourced. Add a machine-readable contamination manifest for the 7/23–8/8 websearch range (the repo already has this exact pattern in data/backfill/mlb/2026/results_close_columns_contamination.json) and have healthcheck.py assert it does not grow. Request tier-1 box dumps for 7/29, 7/31, 8/1–8/5, 8/7 and re-run parse_box_dump.py over them. Until that is done, mark the n=54 cumulative and 31-game paired cohorts PROVISIONAL in progress.md and state.json rather than citing them as gate evidence.

findings.title: The 'structural fix' is not structural — parse_box_dump.py is a standalone script wired into nothing, and healthcheck.py cannot detect a well-formed wrong score
findings.evidence: grep for `parse_box_dump` across the tree matches only the script itself, two JSON provenance strings and the progress.md narrative — there is no reference in /home/user/sports-model/harness/healthcheck.py. healthcheck's results.csv block (healthcheck.py:34-37) checks only row/final counts >=1505, duplicate game_ids, presence of home_win+total, and freshness <=2 days. Every one of the four bad 8/8 rows passed all of those checks. There is no source-tier field, no source-tier gate, and no check that a result's provenance is tier-1.
findings.impact: Nothing prevents the next session from ingesting results via WebSearch snippets again. The commit message for de87ba3 itself identifies this as 'the THIRD instance of the same failure mode' and says 'the earlier fixes were narrative rather than structural' — but the new fix is also opt-in: a tool a future model must remember to invoke, with no enforcement if it doesn't.
findings.recommendation: Add a `source_tier` column to results.csv and a healthcheck assertion that no row dated after a cutoff carries tier>1 without an entry in a declared exceptions manifest. Make the ingestion runbook path 'owner box dump -> parse_box_dump.py -> results.csv' the only sanctioned route, and have healthcheck fail (not warn) on any new row whose source string does not match the sanctioned parser signature.

findings.title: Correcting the data improved accuracy but worsened calibration, and the reason inverts the prior session's headline reading of the model
findings.evidence: Recomputed from cards/2026-08-08_card.json home_wp vs authoritative labels: Brier 0.2558 -> 0.2614 (+0.0056) while the straight-up record went 7/15 -> 8/15. The driver is ATH@BOS, V13's single highest-conviction call of the slate at home_wp 0.614 (card row NC03), which flipped from a win to a loss and alone contributes +0.228 to the Brier sum; the two games V13 newly gets right are LAA@MIA at 0.526 and DET@SF at 0.454 — both near coin-flips. Excess over coin-flip goes from 0.0058 to 0.0114, i.e. roughly double what was reported.
findings.impact: The prior session reported 'Brier 0.2558 still > coin-flip 0.25: model not validated' — directionally right but understating the miss by ~2x. More importantly the corrected shape says something the original could not see: V13's one confident call lost and its record gains came from near-.500 noise. The original's favorable framing ('V13 edged the market on an upset-heavy night', 'compression caught winning dogs') reads as a positive data point when the calibration evidence moved against the model. The corrected file notes the accuracy/Brier divergence but does not revisit the mechanism claim built on it.
findings.recommendation: In the corrected record, state explicitly that the slate's only high-conviction V13 call (BOS 0.614) lost, that both newly-correct games were coin-flips, and that on the calibration metric the slate is worse evidence for V13 than originally reported. The 'compression caught winning dogs (WSH/CWS/TB)' sentence survives literally — all three genuinely won — but should not be carried forward as a favorable mechanism finding when it coexists with a worsened Brier.

findings.title: grading_CORRECTED.json omits the injury-overlay comparator, so pairing it with the surviving original doubles the apparent overlay benefit
findings.evidence: /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading_CORRECTED.json corrects `pass1_marketblind` to 8/12 but has no entry for the raw-V13 evening baseline and no restatement of the original's `injury_overlay_finding`. The superseded /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading.json still reads 'Pass-1 injury adjustment was NET POSITIVE on the evening (7/12 vs V13 raw 6/12)'. I recomputed the raw-V13 baseline on the same 12 evening games: it is also +1, moving 6/12 -> 7/12.
findings.impact: A reader who takes the corrected Pass-1 figure (8/12) and the only surviving raw-V13 comparator (6/12) computes a +2 overlay benefit — double the true +1. The heuristic injury overlay is exactly the kind of unvalidated component that would get promoted on an inflated read, and the per-game attributions are unchanged (deGrom->TEX and ->SD helped, Wood-out->fade-WSH hurt since WSH won 8-2), so the +1 is all there is.
findings.recommendation: Add `v13_raw_evening: {reported: '6/12', actual: '7/12'}` to the corrected file and restate injury_overlay_finding as 8/12 vs 7/12, net +1 at n=1 slate.

findings.title: cards/2026-08-09_card.json was generated from the contaminated results.csv and was neither regenerated nor flagged; the staleness is immaterial but undocumented
findings.evidence: /home/user/sports-model/cards/2026-08-09_card.json was built 2026-08-09T06:00Z (commit c3df775) and is untouched by the correction commit de87ba3 (git log for that path shows only c3df775). harness/daily_card.py:28 derives season RF/RA from every final in results.csv, so the card consumed the bad rows. Measured contamination of the 8 affected teams' season rates: LAA rf_pg -7.55%, SF ra_pg +7.06%, DET ra_pg -7.35%, SF rf_pg -6.25%, ATH rf_pg +5.80%, BOS ra_pg +5.56%, MIA rf_pg +5.19%, LAA ra_pg +5.00%, DET rf_pg +4.88%, MIA ra_pg -4.76%, BOS rf_pg -3.45%, ATH ra_pg -3.28%, TB/SEA ~1-2%. I rebuilt the card in a scratchpad mirror at the as-of-8/9-morning vintage both ways; the reverted build reproduces the committed card exactly on all 15 home_wp values.
findings.impact: Materially small: max |delta home_wp| 0.006 (DET@SF, TB@SEA), zero side-pick flips, proj_total unchanged to 0.1, and the 8/9 grading is 11/15 with Brier 0.2353 (as built) vs 11/15 / 0.2350 (clean) — so the 'V13 11/15, Brier 0.2353' conclusion in grading_CORRECTED.json and docs/progress.md:1587 stands. The problem is provenance, not arithmetic: a frozen card sits on disk computed from a vintage now known bad, with nothing recording that, and the R3-correct choice (leave it frozen) is indistinguishable from the failure mode (forgot to rebuild).
findings.recommendation: Do not regenerate the frozen card. Append a sidecar note (or a line in the corrected grading record) stating that cards/2026-08-09_card.json was built on the pre-correction results vintage, that the effect was quantified at max 0.006 home_wp with zero pick flips, and that the 8/9 grading is unchanged. Consider stamping cards with the results.csv sha256 they were built from so this is mechanical rather than remembered.

findings.title: daily_card.py computes team form with no as-of date filter, which is both the propagation path for this incident and an unguarded look-ahead hazard
findings.evidence: harness/daily_card.py:28 — `# ---- team form + venues from results.csv (as-of everything on disk) ----` — followed by a loop over every row with status=='final' and no comparison against the card's own date. By contrast harness/build_ml_asof.py enforces the invariant explicitly, emitting `team obs {date} NOT strictly before {slate_date}` violations (build_ml_asof.py:249-251).
findings.impact: This is what turned 4 bad rows into 8 corrupted team season rates that then fed a downstream card. It also means the card generator has no defense if results.csv ever contains same-day or future-dated rows: a retro-rebuild of any historical card today would silently use post-game information, producing an inflated result that looks like model skill. The ml_asof path has the guard; the live card path — the one whose outputs get graded and reported to the owner — does not.
findings.recommendation: Add the same strict `date < slate_date` filter and violation check to daily_card.py's team-form loop, and have it record the results.csv sha256 and max observed date into the card JSON so any card can be replayed against its true input vintage.

findings.title: Derived outcome surfaces the frozen card publishes were also corrupted but were never graded, so a future retro-grade of 8/8 will silently use them if it reads the wrong rows
findings.evidence: cards/2026-08-08_card.json publishes rl_home_cover/rl_away_cover, blow_home/blow_away and p_over/p_under/total_lean per game. Recomputed against the corrected results: run-line cover side flips on 3 of 15 games (ATH@BOS HOME -1.5 -> AWAY +1.5; LAA@MIA AWAY -1.5 -> HOME -1.5; DET@SF HOME -1.5 -> AWAY +1.5); blowout events go from 2 to 4 (LAA@MIA becomes HOME>=5, DET@SF becomes AWAY>=5); total leans go 10/14 -> 9/13 because DET@SF lands exactly on the 8.0 line and becomes a PUSH instead of a scored UNDER. Neither 2026-08-08_grading.json nor 2026-08-08_grading_CORRECTED.json scores totals, run lines or blowouts.
findings.impact: No reported number is wrong today, since none of these were graded. But the program does report total leans elsewhere (docs/progress.md:1481, '8/6 V13 total leans 2/7'), so 8/8 is a gap in a metric that is otherwise tracked, and any later backfill of RL/totals/blowout diagnostics for 8/8 would be wrong on 3-4 of 15 games if it reached for a cached figure rather than recomputing from the corrected rows.
findings.recommendation: Record the corrected total-lean (9/13, one push), run-line and blowout outcomes for 8/8 in the corrected grading file so the frozen card's full forecast surface has one authoritative scored record, and note that DET@SF is a total PUSH at 8.0.

agent_findings_by_dimension.dimension: Governance gaps that let a 27%-wrong result ingestion be graded, committed, and reported while healthcheck stayed HEALTHY
agent_findings_by_dimension.summary:
The system's governance is real but is pointed at the wrong surface. Every hard control — the hash chain, the frozen-lineage verifier, the append-only registry, the falsification battery, the policy gate — guards MODEL IDENTITY and FORECAST PROVENANCE. Not one control guards the OUTCOME LABEL, which is the single input every one of those instruments is scored against. `data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv` is an unchained, mutable, free-text-provenance CSV that any writer may edit in place, and `harness/healthcheck.py` asks only four things of it: ≥1505 finals (a monotone floor now at 1776), no duplicate ids, non-empty `home_win`/`total`, and ≤2 days stale (a WARN). All four are satisfied by wrong scores. I ran healthcheck: HEALTHY — 0 fail, 0 warn, and it would have printed exactly that on 8/9 with three winners reversed on disk.

The workflow's postgame step was NOT followed, and could not have been. `harness/runbook.md:30` specifies the tier-1 mechanism — WebFetch statsapi `hydrate=linescore` → upsert — and statsapi has been dead since ~7/24 (last statsapi-sourced row is 2026-07-24; progress.md:1353 logs a 403). For 16 days the system silently substituted a model reading search snippets for the prescribed official feed. AGENTS.md:32 (R8) still reads "All web data via WebFetch tool; verbatim-extraction prompts"; AUTHORIZATIONS.md contains zero occurrences of "WebSearch". No rule was amended, no owner grant recorded, no DEGRADED state declared. "Ingest the official result" (OPERATING_WORKFLOW.md:31-32) became an assumption rather than a verified property — `forecast_states.json` even encodes it as a standing rule ("grade proceeds on the official result") while defining no state in which a result's officiality is checked.

Three controls that would have caught this ALREADY EXISTED in the repo and were not on the path: a cross-source REFUSE gate (`harness/grade_0725.py:23-51`), a per-day evidence file with per-game citations (`data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-07_finals.json` — no 8/8 equivalent was ever written), and a fabricated-hash refusal (`forecast_registry.py:122-131`, forecasts only). This is the third recurrence (7/23 partial capture, 7/29 extra-innings, 8/8), and the 8/07 corrections file names the exact residual risk that then fired. Prior fixes were narrative; they were written into JSON notes and prose lessons rather than into a gate, so each one decayed by the next cycle. Worth noting: the 8/10 tier-1 correction reproduces the same defect one tier up — the authoritative dump is cited by sha256 but is not in the repo, so the correction is itself unreproducible.

findings.title: No source-tier gate: a search snippet grades identically to an official box score
findings.evidence: data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv has 21 columns and none is a tier; provenance is free-text prose in `source` (e.g. "websearch_multi_source(ESPN/MLB.com) 2026-08-09" on all 15 8/8 rows). `grep -rn source harness/healthcheck.py` hits only comments at lines 79 and 88 — no check ever reads the column. The tier ladder (1=official box, 2=recap PROVISIONAL, 3=snippet PROVISIONAL-never-finalizes) exists only in a docstring written AFTER the incident, harness/parse_box_dump.py:16-19, which points at "RESULT_SOURCE_TIER in the results schema" — a symbol that does not exist anywhere in the repo (grep returns that docstring and one JSON key it writes).
findings.impact: The weakest possible evidence class silently acquired the authority of the strongest. Tier-3 rows entered results.csv, were graded, were folded into data/mlb/ml_asof/dataset.jsonl as training labels, and were reported to the owner as validated learning, with no artifact anywhere in the system recording that the evidence was snippet-grade.
findings.recommendation: Add a mandatory `source_tier` column (1/2/3) to results.csv, populated at write time and validated by healthcheck (fail on null/out-of-range). Make grading refuse to consume any row with tier>1 unless it is explicitly marked PROVISIONAL and the resulting grade is likewise tagged provisional. Delete the phantom RESULT_SOURCE_TIER reference or implement it.

findings.title: healthcheck's results.csv block is structurally incapable of detecting a wrong score
findings.evidence: harness/healthcheck.py:29-42 is the entire dataset-integrity surface: line 34 `len(finals)>=1505` (a monotone floor, currently 1776 — it can never fail again and cannot detect deletion of 200 rows), line 35 duplicate game_ids, line 36-37 `home_win in (0,1) and total != ""` (presence, not value), line 38-40 freshness as a WARN. I executed harness/healthcheck.py: "HEALTHY — 0 fail, 0 warn", 40/40 OK. Every one of these passes with the winner reversed on three games.
findings.impact: The session-start gate that AGENTS.md:9-12 makes mandatory before any work returned a clean bill of health across the entire incident — before the bad ingest, after grading on it, and after the in-place correction. Its green light was read as evidence the data was sound, which is precisely the failure mode the gate exists to prevent.
findings.recommendation: Replace the floor with an exact expected-row assertion per date, and add value-level checks: score range sanity, margin==home_score-away_score, total==sum, home_win consistent with the scores, and a cross-check of each final against an independent artifact. A check that cannot fail is not a check.

findings.title: No two-source agreement requirement — and the gate that enforced it already existed and was abandoned
findings.evidence: harness/grade_0725.py:23-51 implements exactly the missing control: it loads two independent captures, refuses any game not status==Final (line 43-44), diffs all 30 team scores, and `sys.exit(1)` on a single disagreement — "cross-source gate : PASS - %d games, %d team scores, 0 disagreements". It was written for one date, never generalized, never called by healthcheck, never referenced by runbook.md or OPERATING_WORKFLOW.md. The 8/8 ingest ran with no agreement check of any kind. In the 8/7 evidence file, 8 of 15 games are single-source or lack a gamePk (data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-07_finals.json) — including LAA@MIA (gamePk null, foxsports only) and DET@SF (gamePk null), two of the three games whose winners were reversed the following night.
findings.impact: Single-source acceptance is the direct proximate cause. The signal that predicts the error — one citation, no resolvable gamePk — was being captured in the evidence files and was never turned into a refusal.
findings.recommendation: Promote the grade_0725 gate to a reusable module on the postgame path: no result may be written unless two independent captures agree on both scores, else the row is written PROVISIONAL and blocked from grading. Treat "single source" and "no resolvable gamePk" as automatic PROVISIONAL triggers.

findings.title: No provisional-vs-confirmed result state; the three-state schema has no state for the result at all
findings.evidence: data/mlb/forecasts/forecast_states.json defines exactly three states — forecast_status, benchmark_status, execution_status — and its standing_rule reads "missing_prices: do NOT prevent outcome grading (grade proceeds on the official result)". Officiality is asserted, never established. docs/OPERATING_WORKFLOW.md:31-32 says "Postgame — ingest the official result. Grade EVERY frozen forecast version" with no intervening verification step. results.csv `status` takes only 'final'/'postponed' (1776/8) — there is no PROVISIONAL value in the vocabulary.
findings.impact: Grading fired the same night on unverified data with no reversibility plan and no way to express "we have a number but do not yet trust it." The system was designed to eliminate permanent-PENDING and in doing so removed the one state that should have held here.
findings.recommendation: Add a fourth independent state, result_status ∈ {PROVISIONAL, CONFIRMED, DISPUTED}, with the transition to CONFIRMED requiring tier-1 evidence or two-source agreement. Grades produced against PROVISIONAL results must be tagged provisional and must not be reported as validated learning or counted toward any cohort.

findings.title: Raw evidence is never retained or hashed — and the tier-1 correction repeats the same defect
findings.evidence: No 2026-08-08 evidence file exists: data/mlb/evidence/websearch/ holds finals files for 7/29-7/31, 8/01-8/02, 8/03, 8/04, 8/05, 8/06, 8/07 — and nothing for 8/08, the day it mattered. The practice lapsed silently because nothing requires it. The 8/10 correction record (data/mlb/evidence/2026-08-10_results_correction.json) cites "sha256": "5e978c3c…" for the authoritative dump, but `find . -iname '*dump*'` returns only harness/parse_box_dump.py — the dump itself is not in the repo, and grep for the hash finds only the record asserting it. Meanwhile forecast_registry.py:122-131 already REFUSES a forecast whose original_file_hash has no artifact on disk ("fabricated hash"); results are exempt from that rule.
findings.impact: The 8/8 rows are permanently unauditable — the claim "websearch_multi_source(ESPN/MLB.com)" cannot be checked because nothing was kept. And the tier-1 correction that supersedes them is equally unreproducible: no one can re-run parse_box_dump.py against the bytes whose hash is published. A hash without its artifact is a claim, not a proof.
findings.recommendation: Require an immutable raw-evidence artifact (the dump, the API response, the paste) committed alongside every ingestion, with its sha256 recorded per row; extend forecast_registry's existing fabricated-hash refusal to cover result evidence; make healthcheck fail when any ingested date lacks a stored evidence artifact whose hash matches.

findings.title: The hash-chained forecast/grade registry — the actual governance instrument — is bypassed by the daily cycle
findings.evidence: forecasts.jsonl slate_dates stop at 2026-08-04 (counts: 07-27:2, 07-28:15, 07-29:16, 07-31:15, 08-03:8, 08-04:15). Nothing for 8/06, 8/07, 8/08 or 8/09. head.json reports 71 forecasts / 69 grades and healthcheck prints "forecast_registry verify: PASS … chain intact". The 8/8 forecasts lived in cards/2026-08-08_card.json and the grades in a loose data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading.json, outside the chain entirely.
findings.impact: The append-only chain verifies only what was put in it; it can never notice what was left out. Because the 8/8 slate was never registered, the incident had no immutable record, no cohort accounting, and — critically — no supersession path when the results were corrected. "Chain intact" was true and meaningless.
findings.recommendation: Make registration the only way to grade: healthcheck should fail when a date has finals in results.csv and a card on disk but no corresponding forecast+grade records in the registry. Coverage of the chain must itself be checked, not just its internal consistency.

findings.title: results.csv is not append-only and carries no chain; the correction mutated four rows in place
findings.evidence: git show de87ba3 -- data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv shows four rows overwritten (LAA@MIA 4-3→0-7, ATH@BOS 3-7→7-3, DET@SF 2-5→8-0, TB@SEA 2-1→3-2). The rows now read `source=CORRECTED_2026-08-10 owner_box_dump(tier1)…` while `ingested_utc` still reads 2026-08-09T05:42:19Z — the timestamp column now misstates when the values were written. R6 (AGENTS.md:30) binds only "the corrections log … append-only", not the dataset. data/mlb/ml_asof/manifest.json hashes results.csv, but that hash is regenerated on every build to match whatever is on disk, so mutation produces a new hash and the rebuild check reports IDENTICAL.
findings.impact: Any of 1,784 rows can be silently rewritten by any writer with no detection. The one place a pinned hash could have caught it is self-updating. Compare harness/verify_lineage.py, which reads inputs at a frozen commit and by design NEVER accepts a successor hash — that pattern exists for model lineage and was never applied to outcomes.
findings.recommendation: Either chain results.csv (head file + sha over ordered rows, checked by healthcheck) or make corrections append-only supersession rows with a `supersedes` field, never in-place edits. Extend R6 explicitly to the results dataset. Never let a manifest hash be regenerated as the only record of a file's content — anchor it the way verify_lineage.py anchors the freeze commit.

findings.title: No per-date completeness check; known partial-capture days are still on file, declared and ungated
findings.evidence: Finals per date in results.csv: 2026-07-23 → 5 games (not 1 missing — roughly ten), 07-27 → 11, 07-30 → 10, 08-03 → 8, 08-06 → 11. data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-07_results_corrections.json states this verbatim under "residual_risk": "partial-capture days still on file: 7/16 (1 game), 7/23 (now 5), 7/27 (11), 7/30 (10)". healthcheck has no per-date count check, and slate files (data/mlb/slates/*_slate.psv) exist for only 7 dates.
findings.impact: Missing games are invisible to every control, and they bias every aggregate silently — a slate graded on 11 of 15 games reports a hit-rate over a non-random subset. The system wrote the risk down and then did nothing that could ever surface it again.
findings.recommendation: Capture and freeze the authoritative schedule per date, and have healthcheck fail when finals+postponed for a date do not equal the scheduled game count. Backfill or explicitly quarantine the known partial days rather than leaving them in the aggregate.

findings.title: Cards use placeholder keys, so no script can grade them and no script can check the grading
findings.evidence: cards/2026-08-08_card.json and cards/2026-08-09_card.json both key all fifteen rows as gamePk NC01…NC15 — invented placeholders, not real gamePks. results.csv 8/8 rows carry a mix of real ids and synthetic ones (7 of 15 are ws0808-*), and 8/9 uses a third scheme (box0809-*). There is no join key between card and result.
findings.impact: Grading a 15-row card was necessarily a manual eyeball match of team abbreviations, which is exactly how four of fifteen can be wrong with nothing catching it. It also forced the R6 violation above: a tier-1 re-ingest of 8/8 would have minted box0808-* keys and duplicated rows rather than superseding ws0808-*, so the corrector overwrote in place instead. Separately, nothing validates that a claimed numeric gamePk resolves to the claimed matchup and date.
findings.recommendation: Require a stable, resolvable gamePk on every card row and every result row, minted once at slate freeze and reused by every downstream artifact; forbid placeholder keys. Make grading a script that joins on that key and emits a per-game table, so the grade is reproducible and diffable.

findings.title: No score-plausibility or self-consistency check at ingestion; the linescore check exists but is off the enforced path
findings.evidence: harness/parse_box_dump.py implements the right idea — innings must sum to the stated final, plus tie/duplicate/self-matchup/game-count guards, with a regression fixture for a header-parsed-as-data false positive. But `grep -n parse_box_dump harness/healthcheck.py` returns nothing: it is not wired into the gate, has no selftest run at session start, and applies only to owner-supplied dumps. Nothing cross-checks any final against the captured total line, the card's proj_total, or team gamelogs. The only independent on-disk corroboration source, data/mlb/team_gamelogs/*.json, stops at 2026-07-22/07-23 for all 30 teams — it went stale when statsapi died and nothing flagged it.
findings.impact: The one structural validation the program now owns is unreachable for the 95% of ingests that are not owner dumps, and it is not exercised by the session-start gate, so it can rot undetected like grade_0725.py did.
findings.recommendation: Add parse_box_dump --selftest to healthcheck, and add cheap plausibility checks that work on any source: margin/total arithmetic, |final - card proj_total| outlier flag, and a winner-vs-market-price surprise flag that quarantines rather than blocks. Refresh or explicitly retire the stale team_gamelogs feed.

findings.title: Superseded artifacts carry no in-file retraction, and grade supersession is convention rather than rule
findings.evidence: data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading.json is unchanged on disk with "v13_straight_up": "7/15", Brier 0.2558, and the "upset-heavy night" narrative, and contains no superseded_by field — only the new 2026-08-08_grading_CORRECTED.json names the old one. In grades.jsonl, two grades now exist for forecast_id P4-20260729-UNRESOLVED:NYY@CWS with contradictory home_win (0 then 1); the later carries supersedes_grade_id by convention, but forecast_registry.validate_records (lines 162-166) checks only that a matching forecast exists — no duplicate-grade rule, no required supersedes pointer, no rule for which grade wins.
findings.impact: An agent or script opening the canonical-looking filename gets retracted numbers with no warning, and any consumer folding grades.jsonl into a hit-rate double-counts and may silently use the stale value. Supersession works only for a reader who already knows the correct file exists.
findings.recommendation: Require a machine-readable superseded_by/superseded_at stamp written INTO the retracted artifact (append-only edit of a status field, or a sidecar the loader must consult), and add a registry rule: at most one live grade per forecast_id, later grades must carry supersedes_grade_id, and validation fails otherwise.

findings.title: Postgame recordkeeping steps were skipped and the freshness checks cannot notice
findings.evidence: Commit 6e436db ("Ingest 8/8 finals … and grade against the card") touched no docs/progress.md — git show --stat confirms 6 files, none of them the journal. grep for "7/15", "0.2558", "6/15" in progress.md matches only inside the 8/10 correction entry at lines 1581-1583; the original 8/8 grading was never journaled at all. state.json.updated_utc is 2026-07-28T20:18:58Z — 13 days stale — despite runbook.md postgame step 5 ("Update state.json.updated_utc + next_actions"); its next_actions still reference grading 7/26 rows. healthcheck.py:207-210 checks progress.md file mtime only; there is no state.json freshness check at all.
