agent_findings_by_dimension.dimension: METHODOLOGY & CLAIM VALIDITY — 2026-08-08 prior-session analytical claims, re-audited against tier-1 corrected results
agent_findings_by_dimension.summary:
I independently recomputed every 8/8 claim from the frozen artifacts under both the ingested (wrong) and tier-1 corrected result sets. The headline aggregates reproduce exactly (V13 7/15→8/15, Brier 0.2558→0.2614, market 6/15→7/15, home 10/15→9/15), and today's correction of those is sound. But the claims that carried the session's *narrative* do not survive, and three of them were already false BEFORE the data was corrected — they are arithmetic and pre-registration failures, not data failures, and today's correction file blessed two of them as "SURVIVES"/"WEAKENED" without recomputing.

SURVIVES (outcome-independent, sound): (1) the compression-toward-.500 DIAGNOSIS — a measured property of the frozen card (mean |p−0.5| = 0.0462 vs market 0.0814, ratio 0.57), true regardless of results; (2) the PASS/$0 decision — made at 22:30Z, before first pitch for all six named candidates, on pre-game information, with $0 at risk; (3) today's explanation of why accuracy rose while Brier worsened (the model's most confident call, BOS 0.614, was the one that flipped) — correct.

VOID: (a) "Pass-1 injury overlay was NET POSITIVE, 7/12 vs V13 raw 6/12" — the frozen overlay differs from raw V13 in exactly two games (CIN@WSH flip HURT, BAL@TEX flip HELPED); they cancel exactly. True net effect is ZERO under both datasets. 7/12 is arithmetically impossible, and today's "8/12" mechanically added +1 to a number that was never verified (true corrected value: 7/12). (b) "attractive plays 3/3 (MIL/CWS/TB)" — no frozen artifact anywhere pre-registers a "Pass-2", an "attractive play", or MIL; MIL was a CAP-excluded game in the pre-board card and a NEGATIVE-EV leg in the post-board one. The actually pre-registered candidate set (slate_decision: CWS/WSH/BAL/HOU/TB) went 3/5. (c) "upset-heavy night" — 7/15 favorites against a market-calibrated expectation of 8.72; P(≤7) = 0.26. An ordinary slate. (d) "recorded as diagnostic evidence toward the promotion gate" — zero 8/8 rows exist in forecasts.jsonl or grades.jsonl.

WEAKENED: "V13 edged the market" is descriptively true on 8/8 (8/15 vs 7/15; Brier 0.2614 vs 0.2751) but statistically null (paired dBrier +0.0137, t=0.81, CI [−0.023,+0.050]) and reverses in context — pooled across the only two slates carrying a market benchmark, V13 is 11/23 vs market 12/23, dBrier +0.0009, t=0.06. The entire +1 margin comes from 5 disagreement games going 3-2, and the grading named only the 3 winners.

The two-pass separation is not audit-verifiable at all: cards/2026-08-08_card.json was OVERWRITTEN IN PLACE (commit 34e8a12, 373 lines changed) when the odds board arrived, injecting market prices and re-running every V13 probability. The genuinely market-blind pre-board freeze scores 9/15 / Brier 0.2594 — a third set of numbers, reported nowhere.

Overall: of the day's claims, 3 survive, 1 is weakened, 4 are void, and 3 of the void ones were void independent of the bad result data.

findings.title: "Attractive plays 3/3" is a post-hoc selection with no pre-registered basis — and today's correction re-blessed it as SURVIVES
findings.evidence: data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading.json:11-18 ("pass2_attractive_plays": 3/3, legs MIL/CWS/TB); data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading_CORRECTED.json:36 ("'attractive plays 3/3' — MIL, CWS, TB all really won"). Repo-wide grep for "attractive", "pass-1", "pass_1", "two-pass", "market-blind": every hit is in the POST-GAME grading file (written 2026-08-09T05:43Z) or the 2026-08-10 correction. Nothing pre-game defines a Pass-2 or names an attractive play. The frozen pre-game record, data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_slate_decision.json, names exactly six candidates — CWS, WSH, BAL, HOU/TB, MLB unders, Portland WNBA — and MIL is not among them. In the pre-board parlay card (commit 6bf2e32) MIN@MIL was CAP-EXCLUDED for unconfirmed starters; in the post-board card (data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_parlay_card.json) MIL is a NEGATIVE-EV leg (fav_ev −0.0983, fav_edge −0.048). Graded on corrected data, the actually pre-registered set goes CWS WON, WSH WON, TB WON, BAL LOST (1-5), HOU LOST (2-3) = 3/5.
findings.impact: This is the single claim the day's verdict rests on ("the disciplined selections cashed", "a clean positive data point for the two-pass discipline") and the one claim today's correction certified as surviving the data fix. It survives only because it was assembled from winners after the fact: a 3-item set drawn from a 15-game slate, including one game (MIL) that no pre-game artifact selected and that the model's own EV screen rated negative. A 3/5 pre-registered record has been reported to the owner and committed as 3/3. Because it is now double-blessed — once by the original grading, once by the correction — it is the claim most likely to be cited later as evidence of method skill, and it is the least supportable.
findings.recommendation: Void the "attractive plays 3/3" line in both grading.json and grading_CORRECTED.json via an append-only supersede. Replace it with the pre-registered slate_decision candidate set graded honestly: 3/5, and note that all five were classified PASS so none was a selection at all. Add a structural rule to OPERATING_WORKFLOW.md: a selection set is gradeable only if it exists in a committed artifact whose commit timestamp precedes first pitch of every game in it; grading agents may not name a selection set that does not already exist.

findings.title: "Injury overlay NET POSITIVE (7/12 vs raw 6/12)" is arithmetically impossible from the frozen overlay; true net effect is exactly zero, and the correction propagated the error
findings.evidence: data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading.json:10,29. Recomputed from data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_updated_card.json (10 rows) plus raw V13 for the two CAP evening games (NYM@PIT, DET@SF), over the 12 evening games (first pitch ≥ 6pm ET) — the same denominator the claim itself uses, confirmed because my raw-V13 evening count reproduces its stated "V13 raw 6/12" exactly under the ingested data. The overlay's adj_home differs in SIGN from raw V13 in exactly two games: CIN@WSH (V13 WSH 0.517 → adj CIN 0.523) and BAL@TEX (V13 BAL 0.492 → adj TEX 0.502). WSH won 8-2, so that flip cost one; TEX won 5-1, so that flip gained one. Net = 0. Overlay = 6/12 under ingested data (not 7/12) and 7/12 under corrected data (not 8/12). grading_CORRECTED.json:20-23 reports "reported 7/12 → actual 8/12", i.e. +1 was added mechanically to an unverified base rather than recomputed.
findings.impact: The injury-heuristic overlay's only claimed empirical support is false, and was false before the results were corrected — this is an arithmetic/reporting failure, not a data failure. The overlay is the newest and least governed component in the stack (a hand-applied heuristic on top of a frozen model), and it has now been recorded twice as showing a measured net gain when the frozen artifact shows it produced exactly one helpful flip and one harmful flip. Today's correction pass, which was specifically meant to re-examine claims built on bad data, did not catch it because it treated the prior session's counts as trustworthy inputs and only adjusted for the four known-wrong games.
findings.recommendation: Supersede both Pass-1 figures: 6/12 as-ingested, 7/12 corrected, overlay net effect ZERO (one flip helped, one hurt) under both datasets. State explicitly that the injury overlay has no measured net effect on n=1 slate. Adopt a standing rule for correction passes: every superseded number must be RECOMPUTED from the frozen inputs, never derived by arithmetic on the number being corrected.

findings.title: The frozen 8/8 card was overwritten in place when the odds board arrived (R3 violation) — the "market-blind two-pass" separation is not audit-verifiable, and the graded numbers are the post-board re-run
findings.evidence: cards/2026-08-08_card.json has two commits: 6bf2e32 (pre-board freeze, all lines/mkt_home_prob null) and 34e8a12 "8/8 evening parlay on owner board" (373 insertions / 373 deletions — a full in-place rewrite, no v2 sidecar, no supersedes record, unlike the 2026-07-29 precedent which used cards/2026-07-29_card_v2.json). The rewrite injected ml_away/ml_home/total, mkt_home_prob, gap_home and total_lean, and simultaneously changed V13 outputs on all 15 rows: 7 games got new starters sourced from the board's probables list (LAD Sasaki→Yamamoto, AZ Kelly→Pfaadt, TB Rasmussen→Jax, SEA Gilbert→Kirby, HOU Blanco→Lambert, SD Ray→King, MIN/MIL TBD→Bradley/Gasser), and the remaining 8 moved by ±0.005 from a fresh n=30000 run. HOU@SD moved 0.504→0.484, flipping V13's pick from SD to HOU. Scoring the genuinely pre-board card against corrected results: V13 9/15, Brier 0.2594 — a third set of numbers appearing in no artifact.
findings.impact: The claimed methodology — market-blind Pass-1, then a separate price check — cannot be verified from the repo, because the artifact that is supposed to embody the blind pass was rewritten in the same step that ingested the prices, at the same path, with the pre-board state recoverable only from git history. The V13 revisions are explainable as legitimate probables corrections plus MC noise, so I found no evidence of actual price-fitting; the failure is that the design makes price-fitting undetectable. It also means the slate has three defensible V13 records (9/15 pre-board, 8/15 post-board, 7/15 as-reported) and the one that was graded was chosen implicitly. R3 ("frozen stays frozen") was violated without a supersede note, and healthcheck's frozen-hash checks do not cover daily cards.
findings.recommendation: Record the R3 violation append-only, with both card states hashed and the three resulting V13 records stated side by side. Enforce structurally: daily cards become immutable at write; a board arriving later produces cards/<date>_card_v2.json with an explicit supersedes field, never an in-place edit. Extend healthcheck to hash every cards/*.json at commit and fail if a card's bytes change after its first commit.

findings.title: "Upset-heavy night" is void, not weakened — 7/15 favorites is an ordinary slate, and the framing was load-bearing for the rest of the narrative
findings.evidence: data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading.json:5 ("UPSET-HEAVY: market favorites went 6/15 (40%); home teams 10/15"); grading_CORRECTED.json:41 downgrades it only to WEAKENED ("still a losing night for chalk but less extreme"). Computed from the 15 mkt_home_prob values in cards/2026-08-08_card.json: sum of max(p, 1−p) = 8.72 expected favorite wins if the market is calibrated. Poisson-binomial over those 15 per-game probabilities gives P(favorites win ≤ 7) = 0.258, and even the wrong figure gave P(≤6) = 0.122. Corrected home teams 9/15, not 10/15.
findings.impact: 7 versus an expectation of 8.7 is well inside one standard deviation — this was a normal slate, not an anomaly. The label is not cosmetic: it is the causal premise for "compression toward .500 caught winning dogs" and for the verdict's structure ("a good night for the method, but an unusual night, so not validation"). Removing it collapses the day's story to "an ordinary slate on which a compressed model went 8/15" — which is what actually happened. Leaving it at WEAKENED preserves a false explanatory frame that will justify the model's dog-heavy tilt on future slates.
findings.recommendation: Reclassify "upset-heavy" from WEAKENED to VOID with the Poisson-binomial figure attached (expected 8.72, observed 7, P(≤7)=0.26). Adopt a standing rule that any "unusual night" label must be accompanied by the market-calibrated expectation and a tail probability computed from the frozen board, or not be used.

findings.title: "V13 edged the market" is statistically null on the slate and reverses once the adjacent benchmarked slate is included
findings.evidence: data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading.json:19 and grading_CORRECTED.json:38 ("V13 edged the market (8/15 vs 7/15) — still true, margin unchanged at +1"). Recomputed on corrected results: V13 8/15, Brier 0.2614; market 7/15, Brier 0.2751; paired dBrier (market − V13) = +0.0137, sd 0.0661, t = 0.81, 95% CI [−0.0229, +0.0504] — crosses zero. The entire +1 margin comes from the 5 games where V13 and the market disagree: CIN@WSH HIT, CLE@CWS HIT, TB@SEA HIT, BAL@TEX MISS, HOU@SD MISS = 3-2; on the other 10 games the two are identical by construction. Pooling with 2026-08-06, the only other slate carrying a same-book market benchmark (data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-06_card_scoring.json: V13 3/8 Brier 0.2537 vs market 5/8 Brier 0.2305): n=23, V13 11/23 Brier 0.2587 vs market 12/23 Brier 0.2596, paired dBrier +0.0009, t=0.06.
findings.impact: A +1 accuracy margin generated by a 3-2 record on five games is reported as the model beating the market, and today's correction reaffirmed it because the margin happened to be preserved. Across every benchmarked slate on file V13 is behind the market on accuracy and indistinguishable on Brier. The grading also named only the three winning disagreements (WSH/CWS/TB) and omitted the two losers (BAL, HOU), which is what makes the compression corollary read as validation rather than as a coin flip. The repo has precedent for doing this correctly — metric_corrections_2026-08-07.json reports a paired dBrier with a t-CI and calls it DESCRIPTIVE — so the 8/8 grading is a regression from the project's own standard.
findings.recommendation: Restate as: on 8/8 V13 was better than the market by 1 game and 0.0137 Brier, paired t=0.81, CI crosses zero, DESCRIPTIVE only; the margin arises entirely from 5 disagreement games going 3-2 (list all five, including BAL and HOU); pooled across benchmarked slates V13 is 11/23 vs market 12/23. Make the paired-dBrier-with-CI format mandatory for any model-vs-market claim, matching the 2026-08-02/08-07 precedent.

findings.title: The 8/8 and 8/9 gradings never entered the governed registry, so "diagnostic evidence toward the promotion gate" is false — and healthcheck reports HEALTHY while blind to all of it
findings.evidence: data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading.json:30 ("Recorded as diagnostic evidence toward the promotion gate"). grep -c "2026-08-08" over data/mlb/forecasts/forecasts.jsonl and grades.jsonl returns 0 and 0. head.json is still {n_forecasts: 71, n_grades: 69}; the last registered forecasts are the 2026-08-04 P4 rows and the last grade is the 2026-08-07 correction. harness/healthcheck.py returns "HEALTHY — 0 fail, 0 warn", including "[OK] forecast registry (71 forecasts, 69 grades, chain intact)" and "[OK] dataset freshness", both of which were equally green while results.csv held four wrong finals.
findings.impact: The 8/8 and 8/9 grading conclusions are free-floating JSON with no forecast IDs, no chain hash, no supersede path and no lineage — the append-only guarantees, falsification tests and gate arithmetic that protect the registry do not apply to them, which is precisely why a wrong number could be written twice and a claim could be re-blessed without recomputation. Meanwhile the healthcheck's green result actively conceals the situation: it validates row counts, duplicates, freshness and chain integrity, none of which can detect either a wrong score or a grading performed outside the registry. This is the structural gap behind the repeat failure mode — 7/23 missing game, 7/29 extra-innings scores, 8/8 four wrong games.
findings.recommendation: Either register the 8/8 and 8/9 forecasts and grades through harness/forecast_registry.py so they inherit the chain and the falsification suite, or strike the "evidence toward the promotion gate" language and label them explicitly UNREGISTERED SIDECAR / NOT GATE-ELIGIBLE. Add two healthcheck assertions: (1) every date with a committed card and committed finals has either registry grades or an explicit recorded exemption; (2) every results.csv row carries a source-tier field, and any tier-3 (search-snippet) row on a date that has been graded raises a WARN until upgraded.

findings.title: WNBA "model ratings 3/3" credits a model the repo says does not exist, counts two explicitly-refused calls as hits, and adds nothing over the market
findings.evidence: data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading.json:21-28. But data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_parlay_card.json states "this system is MLB-only; there is NO WNBA model. Per R1 (never invent numbers) no WNBA probabilities are produced", and data/wnba/analysis/2026-08-08_updated_card.json is classified "No model win prob is fabricated; ratings are log5/Massey (injury-blind)". That same card marks Fever@Sky confidence LOW with "DO NOT PRICE without the official report... genuinely two-way and unresolved", and Storm@Portland was corrected to "mostly MODEL OVERCONFIDENCE" (2026-08-08_massey_overlay_correction.json) then classified PASS in slate_decision.json:"Portland WNBA — Injury-blind rating overconfidence". Against data/wnba/evidence_2026-08-08_finals.json (Lynx 98-87, Fever 90-86, Portland 100-93), the market side also went 3/3: Lynx ~62% fav, Fever ~68% fav, Portland ~56% fav (2026-08-08_massey_overlay.json market_t1 values plus the consensus correction).
findings.impact: Three favorites winning three games is recorded as a 3/3 record for "model ratings" in a domain where the repo has repeatedly and correctly insisted no model exists. Two of the three were calls the session had explicitly refused to make or had classified PASS hours earlier; converting a refusal into a scored hit is the same post-hoc mechanism as the MLB "attractive plays". And because the ratings agreed with the market on all three, the record contains zero information about rating skill. This claim also sits in the same verdict line as the MLB claims, so it inflates the day's apparent success rate with a number that cannot mean anything.
findings.recommendation: Void the WNBA 3/3 line. If a WNBA record is to be tracked at all, register the ratings as a named, hashed identity first, grade only games where the rating and the market DISAGREE, and report the market's record alongside it. Restate that Fever@Sky was explicitly not priced and Portland was PASSed, so neither is gradeable as a rating call.

findings.title: The injury heuristic is not the rule it claims to be — off-menu magnitudes, one sign contradiction, and a credited mechanism the artifact explicitly excludes
findings.evidence: data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_updated_card.json header declares "a TRANSPARENT HEURISTIC (star bat ~4%, regular ~2%, sign toward the healthier side)". The ten applied inj_delta_home values are −0.020, −0.010, +0.040, −0.010, −0.035, 0.000, −0.040, 0.000, −0.010, +0.010: five are off the stated menu (±0.010, −0.035). TOR@PHI applies −0.010 for "Vlad Jr back" (a star bat, menu value 4%). BAL@TEX (lines 157-161) is an outright sign contradiction: the note reads "Josh Jung (TEX 3B) IL small negative for home TEX" while inj_delta_home = +0.010, raising home TEX from 0.492 to 0.502 and flipping the pick — and that flip is the one game credited as "helping". The same note says "deGrom already in SP", i.e. deGrom is explicitly NOT part of the delta, yet grading.json:29 credits the gain to "weighting deGrom->TEX". HOU@SD carries inj_delta_home 0.000 with "raises TOTAL not side" and the overlay picks HOU, which LOST 2-3 — so "and ->SD helped" is false in both direction and outcome. Separately, the CLE@CWS delta of −0.035 rests on "J.Ramirez BACK for CLE", which 2026-08-08_slate_corrections.json disproved the same day (official lineup: Kwan, Adell, DeLauter, Martinez, Hoskins, Rocchio, Bazzana, Hedges, Genao); the overlay was never re-derived.
findings.impact: The overlay's declared virtue is transparency — a rule anyone can re-apply and check. It is not reproducible from its own stated rule on half its rows, the single flip credited with helping was produced by a delta whose sign contradicts its own rationale, and the causal story told about it in the grading contradicts the artifact twice. Compounding this, the overlay's inputs are search-snippet injury reports — the identical evidence class, at MEDIUM confidence with WebFetch egress-blocked (data/feeds/SOURCES_REGISTRY.json), that produced the 27%-wrong results — and one input was already proven false within three hours. So the heuristic is unauditable, its measured effect is zero (see the Pass-1 finding), and its inputs share the failure mode under correction.
findings.recommendation: Record that the overlay is not reproducible from its stated rule; either write the rule down as executable code that emits the deltas, or drop the "transparent heuristic" framing. Fix or void the BAL@TEX sign, and void the "deGrom->TEX and ->SD helped" sentence entirely. Re-derive or annul the CLE@CWS row given the disproven Ramirez input. Require every injury delta to carry its source, source tier and the menu term it instantiates.

findings.title: PASS/$0 is sound and outcome-independent — but the five criteria are structurally unsatisfiable, so "nothing tonight clears all five" reads as a slate judgment it never was
findings.evidence: data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_slate_decision.json (built 2026-08-08T22:30:22Z; "verdict": "Nothing tonight clears all five"). Criterion 4 is "No compression / R5 flag", but compression is a global property of every V13 number on the card (mean |p−0.5| = 0.0462 vs market 0.0814, ratio 0.57), not a per-game condition. Criterion 5 requires "a validated model cohort", and data/mlb/forecasts/forecast_states.json records clean_promotion_n: 0 with gate 0/100 NO_PROMOTE. Timing check: the file is stamped 22:30Z, by which point ATL@NYY (19:05Z), LAA@MIA and ATH@BOS (20:10Z) were final and TOR@PHI (22:05Z) was in progress — but all six named candidates (WSH 22:45Z, CHC/KC 23:10Z, CWS/BAL/HOU 23:15Z, TB 01:50Z, Portland 00:30Z) were still pre-first-pitch.
findings.impact: The verdict itself fully survives the data correction and is the strongest thing the session did: it was made before first pitch for every candidate it names, on information that existed at the time, and no money was ever exposed — the result errors cannot reach it, and today's correction is right to say so. The methodological problem is framing. Criteria 4 and 5 cannot be satisfied by V13 on any slate at the current gate state, so the PASS was determined before the slate was examined. Presenting it as a nightly finding overstates the analysis performed and quietly implies that a future slate might clear the bar, when nothing on the current trajectory can until the gate moves. It also makes the PASS uninformative as evidence: it will read PASS on a slate with a genuine edge exactly as it does here.
findings.recommendation: Keep the decision; relabel it a STANDING STRUCTURAL PASS with the blocking criteria named (compression is global; clean_promotion_n = 0), and state the condition under which the answer could change. Add the qualifier that the artifact was written at 22:30Z with 3 of 15 games already final, and that all named candidates were nonetheless pre-first-pitch. Separate the per-candidate reasoning from the structural blockers so a real edge would be visible rather than absorbed into a blanket PASS.

findings.title: "Brier 0.2558 > coin-flip 0.25, so not validated" is the wrong benchmark for a model this compressed, and the market Brier was never computed
findings.evidence: data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading.json:19. With mean |p−0.5| = 0.0462, a fully uninformative predictor emitting these same probabilities scores Brier ≈ 0.25 + mean((p−0.5)^2) ≈ 0.2526, so the 0.25 threshold is nearly unreachable by construction and carries almost no information about skill. The informative comparison — the market's Brier on the same 15 games — appears nowhere in grading.json or grading_CORRECTED.json; I computed it as 0.2645 as-ingested and 0.2751 corrected, i.e. V13 was better on Brier under both datasets.
findings.impact: The reasoning is invalid even though its direction is conservative: the model is scored against a threshold it cannot meaningfully clear while compressed, which conflates "the slate was hostile to chalk" (the market also scored 0.2751, far above 0.25) with "the model is unskilled". The practical cost is that the one metric that did favour the model on this slate was never computed, while the day's favourable conclusions were instead built on the invented Pass-1 and attractive-plays numbers. Grading that reaches for the wrong benchmark and then supplies unregistered numbers to fill the gap is the mechanism that produced the overreach.
findings.recommendation: State V13 and market Brier together on every graded slate (8/8 corrected: 0.2614 vs 0.2751) with the paired difference and CI, plus a compression-adjusted reference (the Brier a null predictor with the same dispersion would score). Retire the bare "> 0.25 so not validated" comparison.

findings.title: The only genuinely pre-registered, frozen, market-blind selection set on the slate — the parlay card — was omitted from the grading entirely; every recommended parlay lost, and the one honest positive was also never computed
findings.evidence: Pre-board parlay card (git show 6bf2e32:data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_parlay_card.json, generated 17:54:55Z, before the earliest 19:05Z first pitch) recommends top legs BOS 0.609 / CHC 0.602 / ATL 0.579 / PHI 0.573 / CWS 0.564 and combos BOS+CHC, +ATL, +PHI. On corrected results: ATH beat BOS 7-3, KC beat CHC 6-3, NYY beat ATL 5-4, TOR beat PHI 7-5, CWS won 6-3 — top-5 legs 1/5, all three recommended combos dead (2/5 and still all dead under the ingested data). The post-board card's probability parlays (CHC+LAD, +PHI, +CWS) and value parlays (CWS+BAL, +WSH) all lost as well. Neither card is mentioned in grading.json. Conversely, the frozen positive-EV leg set from that same card (CWS +125, WSH +131, BAL +136, HOU +107, TB +105) went 3/5 for a flat-1u paper P/L of +1.61u on 5u (+32% ROI), identical under both datasets — also never computed.
findings.impact: The session graded a selection set it invented after the games and skipped the selection sets it had actually frozen before them — in both directions. The omitted pre-registered record is materially worse than the invented one (1/5 top legs, every combo dead, versus the reported 3/3), so the day's conclusions are not merely unsupported but inverted relative to the evidence the session itself had committed. That the genuinely favourable number (+1.61u on the frozen +EV set) was also missed shows this is a grading-discipline failure rather than deliberate flattery: the grading simply did not go back to the frozen artifacts at all.
findings.recommendation: Grade the frozen parlay card append-only for 8/8: top-5 legs 1/5, all recommended combos LOST, frozen +EV set 3/5 at +1.61u/5u paper, all labelled n=1 and DESCRIPTIVE. Make it a standing requirement that every committed pre-game selection artifact for a date is enumerated and graded, and that the grading file lists the artifacts it consumed by path and commit hash so an omission is visible.

agent_findings_by_dimension.dimension: REPEAT FAILURE PATTERN — data-ingestion / verification failures across the sportsmodel program
agent_findings_by_dimension.summary: The 8/8 ingestion error is the eighth instance of one failure class, not a new incident. The class was formally named on 2026-07-27 in docs/core_breakdown.html §2 — "Summaries are not sources… Five incidents, one root cause, and it keeps recurring because the summary is always the convenient artifact" — and it has recurred at least six more times since that sentence was written. TIMELINE OF RESULT/INPUT INGESTION FAILURES: (1) 7/23 Sale pitcher-log phantom rows; (2) 7/24 accent-sensitive name lookup silently capping arms; (3) 7/25 statsapi linescore served stale + home/away-SWAPPED (KC@DET), caught pre-grade; (4) 7/26 LAD@NYM box-paste SO 8-vs-9; (5) 7/26 aggregator K board mixed best-price-across-books, contaminating 10 of 30 arms; (6) 7/27 fantasy roster call from a truncated display; (7) 8/3 cross-book best-odds de-vig produced an invalid market benchmark for all 8 forecasts; (8) 8/6 three 8/5 scores were 8/4 "echoes", caught in-flight; (9) 8/7 slate enumeration missed 3 of 11 games and named the wrong CIN probable; (10) 8/7 records cross-validation found 7/29 NYY@CWS and CHC@STL stored at WRONG regulation-era scores (both winners flipped) and 7/23 AZ@STL missing entirely — latent ~9 days; (11) 8/8 Jose Ramirez lineup misread (snippet conflated his 8/7 return with 8/8); (12) 8/8 Storm@Portland market direction reversed from a single-book snapshot; (13) 8/10 the 8/8 finals, 4 of 15 wrong with 3 winners flipped, already used to grade the model and report conclusions. QUANTIFICATION: 17 distinct games have required correction across 6 result/slate incidents — 7 games whose recorded result was wrong or absent on disk (5 of them with the WRONG WINNER: 7/29 NYY@CWS, 7/29 CHC@STL, 8/8 ATH@BOS, 8/8 LAA@MIA, 8/8 DET@SF), 4 more caught in-flight before persisting (7/25 KC@DET, 8/5 NYM@CLE, MIN@KC, ATH@CIN), 3 games missing from the 8/6 card, and 3 games with a materially wrong pregame read. CHARACTERIZATION OF THE PATTERN: results are ingested by a language model reading a description of a page rather than the page; the recorded provenance string is self-asserted and never verified; there is no structural cross-check (a score has no internal redundancy the way a linescore does); and detection has been 100% EXOGENOUS — every single result error was found because the owner supplied a better artifact (an odds board on 8/7, a Statcast dump on 8/10), never by healthcheck, the registry, or any selftest. FIXES, STRUCTURAL vs NARRATIVE: the July defects reliably earned code gates (log-integrity scan, accent normalisation, exact-width parser dispatch, ER/BB placeholder manifest, HFA single-source scan, close_* contamination manifest — all live in harness/healthcheck.py). Every August defect earned prose instead: the "echo guard", "owner board is the completeness authority", "same-book de-vig going forward", "never grade from a single endpoint" and "the 7/29 extra-innings lesson is now standard procedure" are all notes in JSON sidecars and progress.md with zero enforcing code. The clearest proof that narrative fixes do not hold: docs/progress.md:1489 (written 8/8) declares the 7/29 lesson "now standard procedure" — the very next ingestion, one day later, was 27% wrong and skipped writing an evidence file at all. The 8/10 fix (harness/parse_box_dump.py) is the first real code since July, but it does not cover the failing path.

findings.title: The new parser does not cover the path that actually fails; the source-tier gate exists only in a docstring
findings.evidence: /home/user/sports-model/harness/parse_box_dump.py:16-19 declares "Source tier (see RESULT_SOURCE_TIER in the results schema): 1 = ... may FINALIZE a graded result; 3 = search snippet ... never finalizes". Grep for RESULT_SOURCE_TIER across the whole repo returns exactly one hit — that docstring line. results.csv has no tier column (header at /home/user/sports-model/data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv:1). `grep -c parse_box_dump` returns 0 in /home/user/sports-model/harness/healthcheck.py, /home/user/sports-model/harness/model_registry.py and /home/user/sports-model/harness/model_registry_pins.json. main() at parse_box_dump.py:237-271 only prints and optionally emits JSON — it never writes results.csv.
findings.impact: The parser only reads the owner-supplied Statcast dump format, which has existed for exactly two days (8/8, 8/9). On any day the owner does not paste a dump — 14 of the last 16 ingestion days — the system falls straight back to the identical unguarded WebSearch-snippet path with no tier check, no linescore cross-check and no selftest in the health gate. The commit message for de87ba3 calls this a "STRUCTURAL FIX", but nothing structurally prevents a fourth recurrence.
findings.recommendation: Add a RESULT_SOURCE_TIER column to results.csv and make it load-bearing: healthcheck FAILS if any row used for grading carries tier 3, and grading code refuses to finalize a tier-3 row. Wire `parse_box_dump.py --selftest` into healthcheck.py alongside the other selftests and pin it in model_registry_pins.json. Give parse_box_dump.py the write path so ingestion is the parser rather than the model.

findings.title: Detection of result-ingestion errors is 100% exogenous — no internal check can see a wrong score
findings.evidence: /home/user/sports-model/harness/healthcheck.py:29-42 is the entire results.csv gate: row count >=1505, no duplicate game_ids, home_win in (0,1), total non-empty, last-final freshness <=2d. All four wrong 8/8 rows passed every one of these. The 7/29 flips were found only by the 8/7 owner-board records cross-check (/home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-07_results_corrections.json:4); the 8/8 flips only by the owner's dump (/home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/2026-08-10_results_correction.json:4).
findings.impact: A wrong score is shape-valid, so the health gate is structurally blind to the only error class that has ever corrupted this program's conclusions. Latency is bounded only by when the owner happens to supply a better artifact: the 7/29 errors sat on disk ~9 days and silently graded two forecasts wrong; the 8/8 errors sat 2 days and produced a full set of reported conclusions.
findings.recommendation: Add a content-level check the system can run itself: recompute every team's W-L and run differential from results.csv and reconcile against an independent record source on every ingestion day (the 8/7 cross-validation, which caught three real errors, was a one-off manual analysis and was never added to healthcheck.py). Fail, do not warn, on any team off by a game.

findings.title: The tier-1 box dump that justified the correction was never frozen to disk — the correction is unreproducible
findings.evidence: /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/2026-08-10_results_correction.json:7 cites `sha256: 5e978c3c83405d0363d0e6b260dc5a0cdd2e3ccc4429c15ac1e85425a9829c98`. Searching the repo for that hash returns only two files that quote it (the correction record and the source column of results.csv). No file with those bytes exists; `git status` is clean, so it was never even left uncommitted. Contrast July practice, where every paste was frozen: /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/box/2026-07-25_paste.txt, 2026-07-26_and_07-28_savant_paste.txt, 2026-07-27_paste.txt.
findings.impact: Four result rows were overwritten and a committed grading was superseded on the authority of an artifact nobody can re-read. `parse_box_dump.py <dump.txt>` cannot be re-run; the "27/30 linescore-verified" claim cannot be reproduced; and if the dump itself were misread, there is no way to discover it. This is an evidence-handling regression against the project's own July standard, made by the very commit that was supposed to fix evidence handling.
findings.recommendation: Freeze the dump bytes under data/mlb/box/2026-08-08_09_owner_dump.txt, verify the recorded sha256 against them, and add a healthcheck assertion that every source string citing a sha256 resolves to a file on disk with that hash.

findings.title: The 8/8 ingestion skipped the evidence file entirely, and stamped a multi-source provenance claim that was false
findings.evidence: Every prior ingestion day wrote one: /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/websearch/ contains 2026-0729-0731, 2026-0801-0802, 2026-08-03, -04, -05, -06, -07_finals.json. There is no 2026-08-08_finals.json — yet the WNBA one for the same night was written (/home/user/sports-model/data/wnba/evidence_2026-08-08_finals.json, added in commit 6e436db). All 15 MLB rows were stamped `websearch_multi_source(ESPN/MLB.com) 2026-08-09` (git show 6e436db -- data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv), a claim of cross-source verification, while 4 of them were wrong and 3 had the winner reversed.
findings.impact: The one day the evidence-freezing discipline lapsed is precisely the day the error rate hit 27%. Because the provenance string is free text written by the same model that did the ingestion, it records an intention rather than a fact — the audit trail actively misleads a later reader into believing those rows were cross-checked.
findings.recommendation: Make the evidence file a precondition: healthcheck FAILS if any results.csv date carries a websearch-class source with no matching data/mlb/evidence/websearch/<date>_finals.json. Restrict the source column to an enum emitted by the ingesting tool rather than free text.

findings.title: No downstream-invalidation tracking: the 8/9 card was built from the contaminated results.csv and its grading headline was never flagged
findings.evidence: /home/user/sports-model/harness/daily_card.py:31-40 builds every team's rf/ra/g form directly from results.csv. cards/2026-08-09_card.json was generated in commit c3df775 at 2026-08-09T06:00:37Z, 18 minutes after the wrong 8/8 rows landed at 05:42:19Z. The 8/9 slate (/home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/slates/2026-08-09_slate.psv rows NC02, NC06, NC12, NC14) repeats all four contaminated pairings: ATH@BOS, LAA@MIA, DET@SF, TB@SEA. Commit de87ba3 does not touch cards/2026-08-09_card.json, and /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading_CORRECTED.json:44-49 reports "8/9 V13 11/15 (73%), Brier 0.2353" with no contamination caveat.
findings.impact: Eight teams' season run-for/run-against were wrong when the 8/9 card was simulated (I measured the as-built error: DET -0.051 RF/g, SF +0.043, ATH/BOS/LAA/MIA ±0.034, TB/SEA ±0.009 — small, roughly 1% of a ~4.3 RPG baseline, but real and unquantified in the record). It matters more than the magnitude suggests because the same correction record states 13 of 15 8/9 games were CAP games, i.e. league-average SP, so team form and HFA ARE the model on those rows. The headline 73% is reported clean when it rests on knowingly-wrong inputs, and nothing in the repo records that dependency.
findings.recommendation: Maintain a derived-artifact ledger: when a results.csv row changes, list every card, dataset and grading built after the bad write and before the fix, and mark each REGENERATED or CONTAMINATED-FROZEN with the measured input delta. At minimum add the caveat to 2026-08-08_grading_CORRECTED.json now.

findings.title: 160 model-mediated final rows have never been independently audited; the two cohorts that were audited failed at 12.5% and 26.7%
findings.evidence: Computed from /home/user/sports-model/data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv: 207 final rows carry a non-statsapi (model-mediated) source. Only 8/8 and 8/9 (30 rows) were checked against a tier-1 artifact; 7/23 and 7/29 (17 rows) were partially cross-validated on the 8/6 board and 3 errors surfaced. That leaves 160 rows across 7/26, 7/27, 7/28, 7/30, 7/31, 8/1-8/7 that no independent source has ever touched. /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-07_results_corrections.json:40 already flags this as "residual_risk" and it was never worked.
findings.impact: On the only clean audited WebSearch cohort the error rate was 4/15 = 26.7%; on the partially-checkable 7/29 cohort it was 2/16 = 12.5%. Applied to 160 unaudited rows that range implies roughly 20 to 43 additional wrong finals sitting in results.csv — the file that feeds team form for every card and the ml_asof training dataset. This is an extrapolation from n=2 cohorts, not a measurement, and should be labelled as such under R1; but it is the honest sizing of the exposure and it is currently unstated anywhere in the repo.
findings.recommendation: Run the 8/7-style records reconciliation across all 30 teams (not just the 22 that happened to be on one board) against an independent season record, and treat any team that does not reconcile as a pointer to the offending date. Until that completes, label the whole 7/20-onward model-mediated span PROVISIONAL in the results schema.

findings.title: The hash-chained forecast/grade registry — the project's own governance instrument — has been bypassed for every slate since 8/4
findings.evidence: /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/forecasts/head.json records n_forecasts 71, n_grades 69. Forecast slate_dates present are only 7/27, 7/28, 7/29, 7/31, 8/03, 8/04. grades.jsonl was last written in commit e149a29 (8/7). The 8/6, 8/8 and 8/9 gradings live instead in ad-hoc files (2026-08-06_card_scoring.json, 2026-08-08_grading.json, 2026-08-08_grading_CORRECTED.json) that no hash chain covers and that harness/test_forecast_registry.py's falsification battery never sees.
findings.impact: The registry exists specifically so a grade cannot be silently restated, and healthcheck.py:134-140 runs its falsification tests on every session. By grading outside it, the last five days of conclusions — including the ones built on wrong data and reported to the owner — carry none of that protection. The 8/8 correction is a superseding sidecar rather than an appended G2-* chain row, unlike the 8/7 correction which did append properly.
findings.recommendation: Backfill 8/6, 8/8 and 8/9 into forecasts.jsonl/grades.jsonl, append superseding G2-* rows for the four corrected 8/8 games as was done on 8/7, and add a healthcheck FAIL when a date has finals in results.csv and a card in cards/ but no registry grade rows.

findings.title: The failure class was named and counted on 7/27, then recurred six more times with no ticket ever opened
findings.evidence: /home/user/sports-model/docs/core_breakdown.html:97-101 titles a section "The failure class that produced five separate errors" and states "Every data error this project has found — every single one — came from trusting something's description of the data instead of the data." Its own §4 gap table (line 242 onward) lists "WebFetch summarization — the only permitted fetch path pipes data through a model, which is the exact thing 'parse raw locally' forbids: unsolved". Meanwhile /home/user/sports-model/state.json known_issues has 30 entries, the newest resolved 2026-07-28 (U02-NONQUALIFYING-LABEL-DEFECT); state.json has not been modified since commit 42794a4 on 7/28. None of the 8/3, 8/5, 8/6, 8/7, 8/8 or 8/10 failures appear there, and the ingestion class has no issue ID at all.
findings.impact: The single machine-readable defect register in the project is 13 days stale and contains no entry for the failure mode that has since produced every material error. A future session reading state.json would conclude the program's open problems are all K-prop board issues from July.
findings.recommendation: Open a standing issue (e.g. RESULT-INGESTION-UNVERIFIED) in state.json known_issues with the full recurrence list and an explicit exit criterion — a code gate, not a doctrine — and make healthcheck warn when known_issues has not been touched in more than N days of active ingestion.

findings.title: A narrative fix was declared "standard procedure" on 8/8 and failed within 24 hours
findings.evidence: /home/user/sports-model/docs/progress.md:1487-1489 (8/8 entry): "Three summary-text-only scores were re-verified via dedicated recap searches BEFORE recording … the 7/29 extra-innings lesson is now standard procedure." The next ingestion, committed 6e436db at 2026-08-09T05:43Z, was wrong on 4 of 15 with 3 winners flipped and wrote no evidence file. The same pattern holds for the 8/5 "ECHO GUARD" (progress.md:1427, and /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/forecasts/reconciliation_ledger_2026-08-06.json:6) and for the 8/3 same-book de-vig "forward_rule" (/home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-03_card_corrections.json:12) — grepping harness/ for same_book / cross_book returns no enforcement anywhere.
findings.impact: This is the cleanest available evidence that a procedure recorded in prose is not a procedure. Every July defect that got a code gate (log-integrity scan at healthcheck.py:95-117, accent normalisation, exact-width parser dispatch at daily_card.py:50-55, ER/BB manifest at healthcheck.py:61-78, HFA scan at healthcheck.py:79-88, close_* manifest at healthcheck.py:51-60) has stayed fixed. Every August defect got a note, and the notes have not held.
findings.recommendation: Adopt an explicit rule that a correction is not closed until either a failing check exists or the record states plainly "no gate — this will recur". Retrofit gates for the echo guard (reject a score identical to the prior day's same-matchup result unless independently reconfirmed) and same-book de-vig (refuse a benchmark whose two prices carry different book attributions).

findings.title: Slate completeness is guarded against a missing DAY but not a partial day — the exact shape of the 7/23 failure
findings.evidence: /home/user/sports-model/harness/build_p4_slate.py:115-132 computes contiguity properly (interior-hole detection over a 14-day window, with a comment citing the 7/29 incident), but only at date granularity. /home/user/sports-model/harness/daily_card.py — which built the 8/6, 8/8 and 8/9 cards — has no completeness check at all. Per-date final counts in results.csv still show 7/16=1, 7/23=5, 7/27=11, 7/30=10, 8/03=8, 8/06=11. /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/forecasts/reconciliation_ledger_2026-08-02_v3.json asserts "contiguity SOLID" over a window containing 7/27=11 and 7/30=10, while /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-07_results_corrections.json:40 lists those same days as unresolved partial captures.
findings.impact: 7/23 held 4 games when a game existed that nobody had recorded, and the ledger reported the window healthy. The 8/6 card missed 3 of 11 games for the same reason on the pregame side (/home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-06_prep_corrections.json:6). Two independent reconciliation records disagree about whether the same dates are gaps, so a reader cannot tell which is authoritative.
findings.recommendation: Record an expected-games-per-date from an authoritative schedule and fail when actual finals differ, rather than inferring completeness from contiguity. Reconcile the conflicting gap claims in the 8/2 and 8/7 records into one ledger of record.

findings.title: Result corrections are applied as in-place edits, inconsistent with the append-only treatment given to grades
findings.evidence: git show de87ba3 -- data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv shows the four 8/8 rows rewritten in place with source `CORRECTED_2026-08-10 owner_box_dump(tier1) ...`; the superseded values survive only in git history and in the prose of /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/2026-08-10_results_correction.json. The 8/7 correction handled the grading side correctly by appending superseding G2-* rows (docs/progress.md:1478), but did the same in-place edit on results.csv.
findings.impact: Minor today because git preserves the prior bytes, but it means results.csv alone cannot answer "what did the model actually see when this card was built?" — which is precisely the question the 8/9 card contamination raises. It also sits awkwardly beside R6, which the project applies strictly to every other artifact.
findings.recommendation: Either add superseded_from / corrected_utc columns so the prior value travels with the row, or state explicitly in the results schema that results.csv is a mutable current-truth view and that as-of reconstruction requires git.

agent_findings_by_dimension.dimension: CONCRETE IMPROVEMENTS — buildable controls to prevent tier-3 result ingestion from finalizing graded conclusions
agent_findings_by_dimension.summary:
The 8/8 failure was not a search-quality problem, it was a **missing gate** problem: every ingredient needed to catch it already existed in this repo and none of them was mandatory. `harness/extract_savant_box.py` has cross-checked linescores against stated finals since 7/29 and was simply not used. Records cross-validation caught this exact failure class on 8/7 (commit e149a29) and `data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-07_results_corrections.json:40` literally says "flagged for the next records checkpoint" — no checkpoint was ever built, and two days later the same failure recurred at 27%. The hash-chained forecast/grade registry (`harness/forecast_registry.py`) is the strongest integrity machinery in the repo, and the 8/6, 8/8 and 8/9 gradings that were reported to the owner never entered it (grades.jsonl stops at 2026-08-04). The 8/8 ingest wrote no evidence artifact at all — every other websearch day has one under `data/mlb/evidence/websearch/`, 8/8 does not.

Three empirical findings sharpen the fix list. (1) I reconstructed the pre-correction 8/8 rows from commit 6e436db and ran a cross-day echo test against 8/7: **DET@SF was ingested as 2-5, byte-identical to the 8/7 DET@SF result, and TB@SEA as 2-1, byte-identical to 8/7 TB@SEA** — two exact fires, zero false positives, catching one winner flip and one score error. A one-run-tolerance variant additionally fires on LAA@MIA (4-3 vs 8/7's 4-2), a second winner flip. So a ~30-line detector covers 3 of the 4 bad rows. The fourth, ATH@BOS 3-7 vs the true 7-3, is a pure away/home orientation flip. (2) The tier-1 dump that authorizes today's correction **is not in the repository** — I hashed every file in the tree and nothing matches `5e978c3c…`; 19 result rows cite a 16-hex-truncated hash of an artifact that does not exist, making the correction unreproducible. (3) 126 result rows across ten dates came from WebSearch; exactly one of those days has ever been checked against tier-1, and it was 27% wrong. ~110 rows carry the entire forward-validation record (the 31-grade paired-Brier cohort in grades.jsonl is sourced `websearch_multi_source(ESPN+MLB.com+BBRef) 2026-08-02`) and have never been audited.

Controls below are ordered by impact per unit of effort. The two cheapest (echo detector, healthcheck wiring) are hours of work and would have caught most of this; the tier column and the registry-gate are the structural fixes that make the failure class impossible rather than merely unlikely. One caveat runs through all of it: `statsapi.mlb.com` is currently egress-denied (proxy status logs `connect_rejected … statsapi.mlb.com:443`), which is *why* the agent improvised — so the control set must make degraded mode safe, not just forbid it.

findings.title: The tier-1 evidence that authorizes today's correction is not in the repo — only a truncated hash of a file that exists nowhere
findings.evidence: data/mlb/evidence/2026-08-10_results_correction.json:7 cites sha256 5e978c3c83405d03…; 19 rows in data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv cite `owner_box_dump(tier1) sha256:5e978c3c83405d03` (16 hex chars, truncated). I hashed every non-.git file in the tree: zero matches. `git log --diff-filter=A -- data/mlb/box/*` shows prior pastes WERE committed (2026-07-25_paste.txt, 2026-07-27_paste.txt, 2026-07-26_and_07-28_savant_paste.txt); commit de87ba3 committed no dump.
findings.impact: The correction is unverifiable and unreproducible. No future session can re-run parse_box_dump.py against the bytes that produced these 19 finals, cannot check whether the parser mis-read a row, and cannot challenge the correction. This violates R1 ("every ledger figure traces to a source") in the very commit that prescribes evidence discipline, and regresses against the repo's own 7/25-7/28 precedent. It is also a strictly worse provenance position than the tier-3 rows it replaced, which at least had a committed evidence JSON.
findings.recommendation: WHAT: commit the raw dump as data/mlb/box/2026-08-08_09_owner_dump.txt, store the FULL 64-char sha256, and add a rule that every hash cited by a result row must resolve to a real file whose sha256 matches. WHERE: the rule already exists in code — harness/forecast_registry.py:122-131 refuses a forecast whose `original_file_hash` has no artifact on disk ("fabricated hash"); lift that block into a shared helper and apply it to result provenance from harness/healthcheck.py. WOULD HAVE CAUGHT: not the 8/8 ingest error itself, but it makes the fix auditable and would have caught the 7/29 and 8/2 websearch cohorts, which cite evidence files loosely in free text. COST: ~1 hour — commit one file, ~30 lines of checker reusing an existing rule. Do this first; everything else depends on evidence actually existing.

findings.title: RESULT_SOURCE_TIER exists only as a docstring comment; nothing in the codebase can distinguish a tier-1 box from a search snippet
findings.evidence: harness/parse_box_dump.py:16-19 declares the tier scheme ("1 = official box … may FINALIZE; 3 = search snippet … never finalizes") but `grep -rn RESULT_SOURCE_TIER` finds no implementation. data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv:1 header ends `…,features_json,source,ingested_utc` — provenance is a free-text `source` column holding 16 distinct ad-hoc strings ('statsapi', 'websearch_multi_source(gamePk-keyed)', 'savant_box_paste(single-source)', 'CORRECTED_2026-08-10 owner_box_dump(tier1) sha256:…'). Every consumer reads it as opaque text: harness/daily_card.py:30, harness/run_v13_historical.py:50, harness/healthcheck.py:31.
findings.impact: No code path can refuse to grade on a snippet, because no code path can tell. 126 of 1784 rows are tier-3 and are indistinguishable from the 1562 statsapi rows to every downstream consumer — the card builder, the historical replay, the ml_asof dataset and the grading step all treat them as equally authoritative. This is the single enabling condition for the 8/8 failure and for every repeat of it.
findings.recommendation: WHAT: append four columns to results.csv — `source_tier` (1|2|3), `result_status` (FINAL|PROVISIONAL), `evidence_path`, `evidence_sha256`. Tier 1 = official box or owner box dump parsed deterministically; tier 2 = reputable outlet recap / single-source owner paste; tier 3 = search snippet or aggregator. Invariant: `result_status=FINAL` requires `source_tier=1`; tier 2 and 3 are PROVISIONAL. WHERE: data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv (appending columns is backward-compatible — all three readers above use csv.DictReader, verified), plus a new harness/results_provenance.py holding the tier map and the invariant, called from harness/healthcheck.py. Backfill is bounded: only 16 distinct existing `source` strings need mapping. WOULD HAVE CAUGHT: the 15 rows ingested on 8/9 for the 8/8 slate would have landed PROVISIONAL, and the grading step (next finding) would have refused to emit 'V13 7/15, market 6/15, lessons learned' from them. COST: 2-4 hours — column addition, a 16-entry mapping table, one invariant function, one healthcheck block.

findings.title: The grading path that produced the owner-reported conclusions bypasses the hash-chained registry entirely, so no 'graded on PROVISIONAL' assertion is even possible
findings.evidence: data/mlb/forecasts/grades.jsonl holds 69 rows, latest slate_date 2026-08-04; forecasts.jsonl holds 71 rows across 07-27…08-04. The 8/6, 8/8 and 8/9 gradings exist only as free-standing summaries: data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading.json is 30 lines of prose aggregates ('v13_straight_up: 7/15 (47%)') with no per-game rows, no forecast_ids, no source hash, no per-game result reference. harness/healthcheck.py runs forecast_registry.verify() at line 136 — which passed clean all through the incident, because the bad grading was never in the registry.
findings.impact: The repo's strongest integrity machinery — append-only hash chain, duplicate-id refusal, cohort rules, the FORBIDDEN_RESULT_KEYS firewall — protected nothing here. It also disabled the supersession mechanism: the 8/7 correction appended proper G2- rows carrying `supersedes_grade_id` (grades.jsonl, last two rows), but on 8/10 no G2 rows could be appended for 8/8 because no G rows existed. Instead a parallel file 2026-08-08_grading_CORRECTED.json was created while the original 2026-08-08_grading.json sits unmodified with no forward pointer, so a future reader picking up the original filename gets the wrong numbers with no signal.
findings.recommendation: WHAT: (a) require every graded slate to go through forecast_registry.append_grade with per-game rows; (b) add `result_tier` and `result_status` to the grade record's REQUIRED tuple (harness/forecast_registry.py:45-48) and add a validate_records rule refusing any grade whose result is not tier-1 FINAL unless explicitly tagged `provisional_grade=true`; (c) add a healthcheck block asserting that no data/mlb/forecasts/*_grading*.json exists without matching registry rows for that slate_date, and that no registry grade resolves to a PROVISIONAL result row. WHERE: harness/forecast_registry.py (rule engine, ~25 lines), harness/healthcheck.py after the block at line 134-140 (~40 lines), plus backfill of registry rows for 8/6, 8/8, 8/9. WOULD HAVE CAUGHT: the 8/8 grading would have been refused at append time, or forced to carry a PROVISIONAL banner, before any of it reached the owner. COST: ~half a day including backfill. This is requested control (6), and it is inert until the tier column (previous finding) exists.

findings.title: A ~30-line cross-day echo detector fires on 2 of the 3 winner flips with zero false positives — three of the four bad rows were the previous day's score for the same matchup
findings.evidence: Reconstructed the pre-correction rows from `git show 6e436db:data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv` and compared to 8/7: DET@SF ingested 2-5, 8/7 DET@SF was 2-5 (exact); TB@SEA ingested 2-1, 8/7 TB@SEA was 2-1 (exact); LAA@MIA ingested 4-3, 8/7 LAA@MIA was 4-2 (one run). I ran the detector: exact-match fires = [DET@SF, TB@SEA] — 2 fires, 2 true positives, 0 false positives; the ≤1-run variant adds LAA@MIA, a second winner flip. These are all same-series consecutive-day games, the exact shape a snippet search confuses.
findings.impact: The cheapest control in this list is also the highest-yield one, and it does not exist. Two exact-duplicate consecutive-day scores in a 15-game slate is a near-impossible coincidence and was sitting in plain view in the file being written.
findings.recommendation: WHAT: on ingest, for each new (away, home, away_score, home_score), compare against the same matchup on the adjacent dates. Exact match → FLAG for re-verification; ≤1-run difference in the same orientation → FLAG at lower severity. Must be a detector, never a verdict — MIN@MIL was genuinely 3-4 on both 8/8 and 8/9 (tier-1 confirmed), so it would fire as a false positive on the 8/9 ingest. That matches the repo's own established convention, stated at harness/healthcheck.py:109 ("Taco validation spec 7/23: dupes/spacing FLAG for reconciliation, never auto-verdict") and harness/runbook.md:80 ("NEVER delete a row on spacing alone"). WHERE: new harness/validate_results.py, invoked by every ingest path and by harness/healthcheck.py over the trailing 14 days. WOULD HAVE CAUGHT: DET@SF and TB@SEA outright; LAA@MIA under the near-match rule. COST: ~30 lines plus a fixture using the real 8/7-vs-8/8 rows as a regression test. Under an hour. Build this today.

findings.title: Standings reconciliation already caught this exact failure class on 8/7, was explicitly deferred to 'the next records checkpoint', and was never built — the recurrence was two days later
findings.evidence: Commit e149a29 ("fix 3 season-data errors found by records cross-validation") used the owner board's `pregame_records` block (data/mlb/odds/2026-08-06_gameboards.json, 22 teams) to find 7/29 NYY@CWS, 7/29 CHC@STL and a missing 7/23 AZ@STL. data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-07_results_corrections.json:40 records the residual risk and the words "flagged for the next records checkpoint". No checkpoint exists: `grep -rn` finds no records-reconciliation code anywhere in harness/.
findings.impact: A control with a proven 3-for-3 detection record on this failure mode was left as a narrative intention. Each of the three 8/8 winner flips moves two teams' records by one game — six teams wrong — which any standings snapshot would expose immediately. The 8/7 note even names the blind spot that bit: 8 teams (LAD NYY SF STL TB TEX COL HOU) were not on the 8/6 board and so were never cross-validated.
findings.recommendation: WHAT: compute cumulative W-L per team from results.csv and diff it against an independent standings snapshot; any team off by ≥1 triggers re-verification of that team's recent games. Snapshots are already available whenever an owner board is pasted (`pregame_records`), and Massey pulls exist under data/external/massey/. Record coverage explicitly — which teams were checked — so untested teams are visible rather than silently assumed clean. WHERE: harness/validate_results.py alongside the echo detector; wire into harness/healthcheck.py as a WARN when a snapshot is <3 days old, FAIL when a mismatch persists across two snapshots. WOULD HAVE CAUGHT: all three 8/8 winner flips, via six off-by-one team records. COST: ~80 lines plus the discipline of capturing a standings snapshot daily. Half a day.

findings.title: Two-source agreement is claimed in prose but never recorded or enforced — and the 8/8 ingest wrote no evidence artifact at all
findings.evidence: `ls data/mlb/evidence/websearch/` lists finals files for 0729-0731, 0801-0802, 08-03, 08-04, 08-05, 08-06, 08-07 — there is no 2026-08-08_finals.json. The 8/8 rows were written straight into results.csv with source string 'websearch_multi_source(ESPN/MLB.com) 2026-08-09' and no backing record. Where evidence files do exist, agreement is unstructured free text: data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-07_finals.json:32 records a single source ('mlb stories 823349') for NYM@PIT while the record_id claims MULTI_SOURCE; 2 of 15 games carry gamePk:null (lines 58, 85) — and those two matchups, LAA@MIA and DET@SF, are two of the four that were wrong the next day.
findings.impact: 'Multi-source verified' is an unfalsifiable claim in this repo: nothing stores which sources were consulted per game, whether they agreed, or what happened on disagreement. The one day with the strongest claim in its source string produced the 27% error rate. Unresolved gamePk correlates with error — 3 of the 4 wrong rows carry synthetic `ws0808-*` ids — and that signal is recorded but never acted on.
findings.recommendation: WHAT: make an evidence artifact mandatory per ingest (refuse to write results.csv rows without one), with a per-game schema requiring ≥2 sources, each with a resolvable identifier, and an explicit `agree: true|false`. Disagreement → PROVISIONAL plus a conflict record, never a silent pick. Add `gamePk_resolved` as a first-class quality flag. Be honest about the ceiling in the doc: harness/runbook.md:83 already notes that StatMuse/MLB.com/statsapi share one upstream, so two-source agreement guards against OUR transcription errors — orientation flips and previous-day echoes, i.e. exactly the observed failure — not against upstream error. WHERE: schema in data/mlb/evidence/websearch/ (extend the existing shape), validator in harness/validate_results.py, enforcement in harness/healthcheck.py. WOULD HAVE CAUGHT: ATH@BOS 3-7 vs 7-3 is precisely what a second independent read resolves; and the missing 8/8 evidence file would have blocked the ingest outright. COST: ~100 lines of schema and validator; the real cost is agent query discipline at ingest time. This is requested control (2).

findings.title: No automatic re-grade or supersession on result change — and corrupted results silently contaminated the next day's forecasts, not just the grading
findings.evidence: harness/daily_card.py:28-36 aggregates team runs-for/runs-against from EVERY final row in results.csv with no date, tier or status filter, then feeds team_rf/team_ra into the simulation. The 8/9 card (commit c3df775, "team form current through 8/8") was therefore built on DET credited with 2 runs instead of 8, SF with 0 allowed instead of 8, MIA with 3 instead of 7, and three inverted outcomes. The correction on 8/10 superseded the grading but did not rebuild that card. The supersession mechanism itself exists and works — grades.jsonl carries G2- rows with `supersedes_grade_id` from the 8/7 fix — but was applied by hand.
findings.impact: A result correction has a blast radius the repo does not track: grade rows, cohort metrics (paired dBrier, cumulative Brier n=54), the ml_asof dataset, and any card built after the bad ingest. Today only the first was handled. The 8/9 card's forecasts were generated from contaminated team form and were then graded 11/15 — a number now resting on inputs that were known-wrong at generation time.
findings.recommendation: WHAT: harness/regrade_on_result_change.py that takes a results.csv diff and (a) appends superseding G2-/G3- grade rows via forecast_registry.append_grade for every affected game, (b) recomputes every affected cohort metric, (c) enumerates and marks stale downstream artifacts — cards whose build time postdates the bad ingest, ml_asof vintage, docs/progress.md claims — and (d) writes a machine-readable `superseded_by` pointer INTO the original artifact's sidecar so a reader who opens 2026-08-08_grading.json is told it is void. WHERE: new harness/regrade_on_result_change.py reusing forecast_registry.append_grade; ml_asof already hashes results.csv wholesale (data/mlb/ml_asof/manifest.json `source_hashes.results`) so its invalidation is free. WOULD HAVE CAUGHT: nothing at ingest — this is the containment control. It would have made today's cleanup complete rather than partial, and would flag the 8/9 card as built-on-corrupt-inputs. COST: ~150 lines plus a supersession-pointer convention. One day. This is requested control (5).

findings.title: ~110 tier-3 result rows have never been audited against any authoritative source, and the entire forward-validation record rests on them
findings.evidence: 126 of 1784 results.csv rows carry websearch provenance, spread over 2026-07-23 (1), 07-29 (16), 07-31 (15), 08-01 (15), 08-02 (15), 08-03 (8), 08-04 (15), 08-05 (15), 08-07 (15), 08-08 (11 remaining). Only 8/8 has ever been fully checked against tier-1 — 27% wrong. The 8/6 board records cross-check covered 22 of 30 teams and found 3 more errors. grades.jsonl's largest cohort (31 rows) is sourced `websearch_multi_source(ESPN+MLB.com+BBRef) 2026-08-02`, and commit e149a29's message reports the paired dBrier +0.00304 and cumulative Brier n=54 computed on it.
findings.impact: Every quantitative claim in the forward-validation record — candidate-vs-market paired Brier, the 31-game cohort, cumulative n=54 — is computed on a population whose only audited sample was 27% wrong with 20% winner-flips. At that error rate the sign of a +0.003 dBrier is not defensible. This is not a hypothetical exposure: three errors have already been confirmed in this cohort (7/29 x2, 7/23 missing) plus four on 8/8.
findings.recommendation: WHAT: request owner box dumps covering 2026-07-29 through 2026-08-07, re-parse deterministically, and run the supersession pipeline. Until that completes, tag the affected cohort metrics as tier-3-derived wherever they are quoted (state.json, docs/progress.md, reconciliation ledgers) rather than letting them stand unqualified. WHERE: data/mlb/box/ for the dumps; harness/parse_box_dump.py to parse; harness/regrade_on_result_change.py to propagate; a known_issue entry in state.json to track the backlog. WOULD HAVE CAUGHT: this is remediation of accumulated exposure, not prevention. It is high priority because the exposure is currently unquantified and is being cited as evidence. COST: owner time to supply dumps; ~2 hours of agent work per date once they arrive.

findings.title: The new parser is not wired into any ritual — exactly how the previous linescore-checking parser came to be ignored on 8/8
findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'parse_box_dump\|extract_savant_box' harness/healthcheck.py harness/runbook.md docs/OPERATING_WORKFLOW.md` returns nothing. harness/parse_box_dump.py:184-235 has a good selftest with a real regression fixture; nothing runs it. Meanwhile harness/extract_savant_box.py:10-14 has cross-checked "the line-score row R totals … against the score line" since 7/29 and was not used for the 8/8 ingest. There are now three overlapping box parsers: parse_box_0725.py, extract_savant_box.py, parse_box_dump.py.
findings.impact: A tool that is not in the session-start ritual does not get used — that is the actual causal mechanism of this incident, not the absence of tooling. parse_box_dump.py will rot the same way: its selftest can silently break, and the next session under time pressure will improvise again. Three parsers with divergent team-name maps is also a live correctness risk (parse_box_dump.py:39-51 maps 'Athletics Athletics'→ATH; extract_savant_box.py uses a nickname map).
findings.recommendation: WHAT: (a) add `python3 harness/parse_box_dump.py --selftest` to harness/healthcheck.py following the existing subprocess pattern at lines 119-165 — 3 lines; (b) name the deterministic parser as the ONLY sanctioned ingest path in harness/runbook.md#postgame and in docs/OPERATING_WORKFLOW.md's postgame step 5; (c) consolidate the three parsers onto one shared team-name map and one linescore checker. WHERE: harness/healthcheck.py, harness/runbook.md:28-46, docs/OPERATING_WORKFLOW.md:31-32. WOULD HAVE CAUGHT: had extract_savant_box.py's linescore check been mandatory since 7/29, the 8/8 ingest could not have been finalized from snippets, which carry no linescore at all. COST: 15 minutes for (a), an hour for (b), half a day for (c). Do (a) and (b) immediately. This is requested control (7), completed.

findings.title: The freshness check actively rewards filling results.csv with tier-3 data when the tier-1 path is blocked, and no degraded-mode procedure exists
findings.evidence: harness/healthcheck.py:40 warns whenever the newest final is >2 days old. harness/runbook.md:30-32 prescribes the only documented ingest path: `WebFetch …statsapi.mlb.com/api/v1/schedule?…hydrate=linescore,venue`. That host is hard-blocked — the proxy status endpoint currently reports `{"kind":"connect_rejected","detail":"gateway answered 403 to CONNECT","host":"statsapi.mlb.com:443"}`, and data/feeds/SOURCES_REGISTRY.json:4 documents EGRESS_BLOCKED across FanGraphs, Savant, B-Ref, Rotowire and Massey. The runbook documents no fallback.
findings.impact: The system's own health gate created pressure to make the dataset current, the sanctioned path was unavailable, and the procedure was silent on what to do — so the agent improvised WebSearch snippets and the check went green. Any control set that forbids tier-3 ingestion without providing a safe degraded mode will simply be routed around again under the same pressure.
findings.recommendation: WHAT: (a) let the freshness check be satisfied by PROVISIONAL rows so there is no incentive to fake finality; (b) add a separate, FAIL-level check for tier-1 finalization backlog exceeding N days, which is the condition that actually matters; (c) write the degraded-mode procedure into runbook.md#postgame explicitly — ingest as PROVISIONAL with an evidence artifact, open a `RESULT-TIER1-PENDING` entry in state.json.known_issues, and request a box dump from the owner in the session summary; (d) state plainly that a PROVISIONAL slate may be carded but may not be graded or reported as a model result. WHERE: harness/healthcheck.py:40, harness/runbook.md:28-52, state.json known_issues. WOULD HAVE CAUGHT: it reframes the incentive that produced the incident; the agent would have had a correct, low-friction action available. COST: ~2 hours.

findings.title: Structural validation has no counterpart to check orientation or slate completeness against — the frozen slate file is never used at ingest
findings.evidence: harness/parse_box_dump.py:157-177 validates ties, duplicates, self-matchups and count-per-date, and 133-154 validates linescore sums — good, but all self-referential to the dump. Nothing compares an ingest against the frozen slate: data/mlb/slates/2026-08-08_slate.psv exists and was never consulted. The 7/23 failure mode was a game missing entirely (data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-07_results_corrections.json:28-30, "7/23 was a partial-capture day: 4 games on file"), and 2026-08-07_results_corrections.json:40 lists four more partial-capture days still on file: 7/16 (1 game), 7/23 (now 5), 7/27 (11), 7/30 (10).
findings.impact: Two of the three historical instances of this failure class are completeness failures, not accuracy failures, and completeness is checkable for free against a file the repo already writes every morning. The ATH@BOS orientation flip is likewise only detectable against an external statement of who is home.
findings.recommendation: WHAT: extend harness/validate_results.py with (a) slate reconciliation — every game in data/mlb/slates/DATE_slate.psv must have exactly one result row and vice versa, with postponements recorded explicitly rather than silently absent; (b) orientation check — home/away in the result must match the frozen slate, and venue must match the home team's park (venue is already carried in results.csv); (c) cheap sanity rules — hits ≥ runs where hits are available, no ties, score range plausible. WHERE: harness/validate_results.py, reading data/mlb/slates/*.psv and data/backfill/mlb/2026/park_factors.json. WOULD HAVE CAUGHT: the 7/23 missing game and the 7/16/7/27/7/30 partial captures immediately. Honestly, it would NOT alone have caught the three 8/8 flips — snippets carry no linescore, and both teams' venues were correct — which is why the echo detector and the tier gate matter more. COST: ~120 lines. This is requested control (3), extended past what parse_box_dump.py already covers.

findings.title: Restoring one allowlisted host would eliminate the failure class outright — 88% of the dataset already came from it
findings.evidence: 1562 of 1784 results.csv rows carry source 'statsapi'. The current denial is recorded verbatim in the proxy status endpoint (`connect_rejected`, `statsapi.mlb.com:443`). /root/.ccr/README.md is explicit: 403/407 are organization policy, must not be routed around, and should be reported rather than retried.
findings.impact: Every control above is compensating for the loss of a deterministic, structured, authoritative feed that this project used successfully for the bulk of its history. With statsapi reachable, result ingestion becomes a scripted fetch with linescore hydration — no model in the loop, no snippets, no tier ambiguity — and the whole class of failure disappears rather than being detected after the fact.
findings.recommendation: WHAT: raise an explicit allowlist request for statsapi.mlb.com (and, secondarily, baseballsavant.mlb.com) with the owner/admin, citing the 27% error rate measured on the fallback path as the business justification. Track it as a known_issue in state.json with an owner and a deadline, consistent with the operating workflow's no-indefinite-PENDING rule (docs/OPERATING_WORKFLOW.md:54-55). Keep the owner-dump path as the permanent documented fallback regardless — network access should never be a single point of failure for grading integrity. WHERE: state.json known_issues; docs/OPERATING_WORKFLOW.md implementation-status table. WOULD HAVE CAUGHT: everything — the 8/8 ingest would have been a scripted statsapi pull with hydrated linescores. COST: near zero to ask; the unblocking is outside the agent's control, which is exactly why the compensating controls above must be built in parallel rather than waiting on it.

findings.title: Derived datasets carry no per-row provenance, so tier-3 contamination cannot be excluded from a benchmark — despite an exact precedent for this pattern in the repo
findings.evidence: data/mlb/ml_asof/manifest.json hashes results.csv wholesale (`source_hashes.results`), which correctly invalidates the vintage on any correction, but dataset.jsonl rows carry no tier, so no consumer can filter. The repo already solved this shape of problem once: data/backfill/mlb/2026/results_close_columns_contamination.json declares a contaminated column range machine-readably, and harness/healthcheck.py:53-60 FAILs if the contaminated set grows undeclared ("is it a real close, or another opening?").
findings.impact: Benchmark claims cannot be recomputed on tier-1-only rows to see whether they survive, which is the first question anyone should ask of the +0.00304 paired dBrier. And the tier-3 population can grow silently, exactly as the close_* contamination could before its manifest existed.
findings.recommendation: WHAT: propagate `source_tier`/`result_status` into ml_asof rows, and add data/backfill/mlb/2026/results_tier_manifest.json declaring which dates and rows are non-tier-1, with a healthcheck block that FAILs when undeclared tier-3 rows appear — a direct copy of the close_* pattern at harness/healthcheck.py:53-60. Then report every cohort metric twice: all-rows and tier-1-only. WHERE: harness/build_ml_asof.py, data/backfill/mlb/2026/, harness/healthcheck.py. WOULD HAVE CAUGHT: nothing at ingest; it makes the damage measurable and stops the contaminated population from growing unnoticed. COST: ~2 hours, mostly copying an existing, already-tested pattern.
