adversarial_verifications.title: Verbatim prior-day echo: DET@SF and TB@SEA ingested as exact copies of the 8/7 finals
adversarial_verifications.reasoning:
CONFIRMED. Every load-bearing claim reproduces from primary sources; I found corroboration the finding did not cite that makes it stronger, not weaker.

VERIFIED FACTS
1. Data. At commit 6e436db, data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv contains exactly the cited rows: `mlb:2026:ws0808-DETSF,2026-08-08,final,DET,SF,2,5` against `mlb:2026:ws0807-DETSF,2026-08-07,final,DET,SF,2,5`, and `mlb:2026:ws0808-TBSEA,2026-08-08,final,TB,SEA,2,1` against `mlb:2026:823103,2026-08-07,final,TB,SEA,2,1`. Byte-identical score pairs on consecutive dates.
2. Source notes. data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-07_finals.json carries verbatim "espn recap 401816435 + b-ref SFN202608070 + CBS DET@SF (SF 5-2 Oracle)" and "mlb gameday 823103 (TB 2-1)". The b-ref key SFN2026080-7-0 does encode 2026-08-07.
3. Authoritative values. data/mlb/evidence/2026-08-10_results_correction.json gives DET@SF 2-5 -> 8-0 (winner_flipped true, linescore_verified true) and TB@SEA 2-1 -> 3-2 (winner_flipped false, linescore_verified null).
4. Statistics. My independent scan of the full 2026 file at 6e436db: 1127 consecutive-day same-matchup pairs, 22 exact-score duplicates = 1.95%, 19 of them statsapi-era. The check fires on 8/8 with exactly 2 alarms, DET@SF and TB@SEA. The burden claim also holds precisely: 19 alarming slates out of 112 dated slates = one alarming slate every 5.9, i.e. "roughly one alarm every six slates."
5. Enforcement gap. harness/healthcheck.py:29-42 is the entire results.csv integrity surface (finals>=1505, no duplicate game_ids, home_win/total presence, freshness warn). The only dup check is on game_id strings, and ws0807-DETSF vs ws0808-DETSF are distinct, so it structurally cannot fire. Grep across harness/ finds no consecutive-day score comparison anywhere.

CORROBORATION BEYOND THE FINDING
data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-05_finals.json contains an explicit `echo_guard` field: "three first-pass scores were 8/4-echoes and were CORRECTED by dedicated recap searches before recording: NYM@CLE 6-5(10) not 6-2; MIN@KC 2-1 not 8-6; ATH@CIN 3-2 not 5-4. PIT@MIL 4-2 verified genuinely identical on both nights." The mechanism was therefore already observed three times in a single night, named by the program, and caught only by manual recap searches. It exists nowhere in code. Further, no data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-08_finals.json exists at all, so on 8/8 the recap-recheck discipline documented in the 8/5 and 8/7 files was dropped entirely. Independently, both echoed games sit in the synthetic-gamePk cohort (8 of the 15 8/8 rows lack a gamePk), a second already-recorded signal that no authoritative gameday page was opened.

ADVERSARIAL TESTS THE FINDING SURVIVES
- Coincidence: all 15 games on 8/8 were 8/7 series continuations. At the measured 1.95% base rate, expected repeats = 0.29, so P(>=2) ~ 3.4%; times P(two randomly chosen pairs both landing in the 4-wrong set) = C(4,2)/C(15,2) = 5.7% gives ~0.2% joint. Not tenable.
- Read-the-right-page-but-misread: dead for DET@SF. Ingested 2-5 shares no digits with the truth 8-0 and reverses the winner, yet is byte-identical to 8/7. Transcription error cannot produce that; reconstruction from the prior recap can.

CAVEATS (do not change the verdict)
- The causal pathway in the impact text ("the search layer returns the prior recap for an identical query") is an inference, not documented: with no 8/8 evidence file, there is no record of what the 8/8 search actually hit. An internal carry-forward of the session's own 8/7 row is an equally consistent path. The echo itself is proven from the data; only the pathway is inferred, and the recommendation is unaffected either way.
- TB@SEA is the softer of the two: its correction is the single one in the correction file with linescore_verified null, and 2-1 vs truth 3-2 is at least conceivable as sloppy transcription. DET@SF alone is sufficient to confirm the finding.
- The recommendation's literal wording "FAIL if identical" is stricter than warranted: 19 of 22 historical alarms are genuine statsapi repeats, and the 8/5 echo_guard explicitly verified PIT@MIL 8/4->8/5 (2-4) as a genuine back-to-back identical result. The finding's own prose resolves this ("each alarm requires only a dedicated recap re-check before the row may be written"), so this is internal wording tension, not an error. Correct implementation is a blocking flag requiring verification, ideally scoped to non-tier-1 ingestion.
- Scope is honestly stated: the check explains 2 of the 4 bad rows and would miss ATH@BOS (orientation flip, 7-3 -> 3-7) and LAA@MIA (4-3 vs truth 0-7). The finding claims exactly that and does not overreach.

Read-only respected: no files modified.

adversarial_verifications.title: CONFIRMED: healthcheck results block passes unchanged on the 27%-wrong 8/8 ingest; two bad rows were byte-identical copies of the prior day
adversarial_verifications.reasoning:
VERDICT: CONFIRMED — and the finding understates its own strongest evidence.

## 1. The quoted evidence is exact

## 2. Concrete failure constructed and executed
I recovered the pre-correction data from git commit `6e436db` ("Ingest 8/8 finals (WNBA+MLB) and grade against the card") and replayed the exact lines 29-42 against it as-of 2026-08-09:

```
[OK ] results.csv rows=1769 finals=1761 (>=1505)
[OK ] no duplicate game_ids
[OK ] all finals have home_win+total
[OK ] dataset freshness: last final 2026-08-08 (1d old)
RESULTS BLOCK VERDICT: PASS (no FAIL)

All four pass on the 27%-wrong slate. The gate's output is identical before and after correcting three wrong winners.

## 3. The duplicate-id argument is stronger than stated
The finding says ws0807-DETSF and ws0808-DETSF are "distinct strings". True, but the actual rows are worse — two of the four bad rows are byte-identical carry-forwards of the previous day's line:

- `ws0807-DETSF ... DET,SF,2,5,1,3,7` (8/7) vs `ws0808-DETSF ... DET,SF,2,5,1,3,7` (8/8)
- `823103 ... TB,SEA,2,1,0,-1,3` (8/7) vs `ws0808-TBSEA ... TB,SEA,2,1,0,-1,3` (8/8)

The corruption was mechanically detectable by string equality on the score columns. The existing check cannot see it because it keys on `game_id` — a synthetic string minted per-date — rather than on (matchup, date, score).

## 4. Counter-hypothesis tested and rejected
No other control validates outcome content. `grep away_score|home_score` across harness/ shows every consumer either writes rows (backfill_results_savant, grade_*, extract_*) or reads them as inputs (build_p4_slate.py:76, daily_card.py:32, build_ml_asof.py:205) — none validates them. forecast_registry.py validates hash-chain, model_id/rng_policy identity, ledger_eligible, result-fields-leaking-into-payload, and artifact-hash existence: all provenance of the MODEL, none of the OUTCOME. The impact statement is if anything understated — the wrong rows also propagated into data/mlb/ml_asof/dataset.jsonl (the correction had to rewrite 23 lines of it), and ml_asof's byte-identical-rebuild check validated them perfectly, because determinism confirms that the same wrong input yields the same wrong output.

## 5. Recommendations — grounded, with two precision caveats
(1) **Consecutive-day duplicate score** — I implemented and ran it. On the wrong data it fires on exactly TB@SEA and DET@SF for 8/8; both vanish in the corrected data. CAVEAT: season-wide base rate is ~20 genuine repeats (e.g. MIN@MIL 3-4 on 8/8→8/9 is real in the corrected file). It must be a WARN/reconcile flag, not a FAIL — matching the repo's own existing idiom at healthcheck.py:109 ("dupes/spacing FLAG for reconciliation, never auto-verdict"). Per-slate it is high-signal: 2 hits on 15 games, both true positives.

(2) **Linescore-sum reconciliation** — genuinely implemented at harness/parse_box_dump.py:133-154, with tie, duplicate-matchup, self-matchup and game-count guards plus a regression fixture against a header-parsed-as-data false positive. `grep parse_box_dump harness/healthcheck.py` returns nothing — not wired in, no selftest at session start. CAVEAT: it only works where the source supplies innings, so it could not have caught the 8/8 websearch ingest by itself. It prevents recurrence only if paired with making the parser the sole sanctioned ingestion route.

(3) **Evidence file per date** — confirmed. data/mlb/evidence/websearch/ holds finals for 7/29-7/31, 8/01-02, 8/03, 8/04, 8/05, 8/06, 8/07 and then stops: there is no 2026-08-08 file anywhere. Fifteen rows were written with zero evidence artifact and nothing complained. Note the repo already has this exact pattern for forecasts (forecast_registry.py:122-131 rejects an `original_file_hash` with no artifact on disk as a "fabricated hash") — results are simply exempt.

(4) **Slate coverage** — I implemented and ran it. 7/29 shows slate 16 games vs 15 result rows (the .psv has no header; line 1 is `NA01|PHI|MIA|...`), so it does fire on the real historical miss. CAVEAT: 8/06 shows slate 8 vs 11 results (the board paste covered more games than the frozen slate), so the assertion must be one-directional — every slate game needs a result, extra results are fine — or it will false-positive.

## 6. Severity
CRITICAL is right for the control gap. One mitigating fact for the writeup: per 2026-08-08_grading_CORRECTED.json both slates were PASS/$0 and the gate stayed 0/100, so no money was ever at risk. The realized damage is to the evidence base (grades.jsonl, the cumulative cohort, the ml_asof dataset) and to conclusions reported to the owner — not to the ledger. The gap itself remains critical because grading a model against outcomes is the system's entire purpose, and the outcome channel is the one input with no validation at all.

adversarial_verifications.title: CONFIRMED: no MLB evidence artifact exists for 8/8 in any commit; the discarded per-game source ids would have caught two verbatim day-over-day echoes
adversarial_verifications.reasoning:
Every load-bearing claim verified independently from the artifacts; the impact reasoning is not only correct but understated.

## 1. The evidence artifact does not exist — and never did

`git show --name-only 6e436db` lists exactly the six files the finding names: `data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv`, `data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading.json`, `data/mlb/ml_asof/{dataset.jsonl,exclusions.json,manifest.json}`, `data/wnba/evidence_2026-08-08_finals.json`. No MLB evidence file.

I went further than the finding: `git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only -- 'data/mlb/evidence/*'` shows every MLB results-evidence file ever added — 7/29-7/31, 8/1-8/2, 8/3, 8/4, 8/5, 8/6, 8/7, plus the 8/10 correction record. **No 8/8 file was ever created on any branch, in any commit.** `git status` is clean, so it is not sitting untracked either. 8/8 is the only slate ingested without one, and the WNBA half of the same commit *did* get `/home/user/sports-model/data/wnba/evidence_2026-08-08_finals.json` — so the omission is specific to the 15 MLB games that were then used to grade the model.

The only surviving provenance is exactly as stated: the CSV cell `websearch_multi_source(ESPN/MLB.com) 2026-08-09` on all 15 rows in `/home/user/sports-model/data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv`. Nothing else carries it — `/home/user/sports-model/data/feeds/2026-08-08_reconciliation.json` is a pregame feed advisory built 19:10Z (hours before first pitch results); `docs/progress.md` was not touched by 6e436db; `/home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/ml_asof/manifest.json` records only a sha256 of results.csv, which hashes the wrong numbers rather than their sourcing.

## 2. The echo is real, and stronger than the finding claims

Reconstructing the as-committed 8/8 rows from `git show 6e436db:data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv` and diffing against the 8/7 rows for the same matchups (8/8 was the same 15 pairings):

- **DET@SF: 8/7 ingested 2-5, 8/8 ingested 2-5 — byte-identical. Authoritative 8/8: 8-0 DET.**
- **TB@SEA: 8/7 ingested 2-1, 8/8 ingested 2-1 — byte-identical. Authoritative 8/8: 3-2.**
- LAA@MIA: 8/7 4-2 LAA, 8/8 "4-3 LAA" — same away score, same winner, matches no real game. Authoritative: 0-7 MIA.
- ATH@BOS: same winner as 8/7 (BOS); the ingested 3-7 is the exact reversal of the true 7-3.

The two exact duplicates are two of the four wrong games. Only two rows in the entire 15-game slate are day-over-day duplicates, and both are errors — this is not coincidence.

The proposed guard would have fired on both. `/home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-07_finals.json` records, for DET@SF, `"espn recap 401816435 + b-ref SFN202608070 + CBS DET@SF (SF 5-2 Oracle)"`, and for TB@SEA, `"mlb gameday 823103 (TB 2-1)"`. Any 8/8 record citing those ids for the same matchup is definitionally an echo — `SFN202608070` even embeds the date. Because no 8/8 record was written, that comparison was impossible. This is precisely the "verification left no trace it was attempted" failure.

## 3. Nothing in the system enforces or detects the omission

`harness/healthcheck.py` reads results.csv only for row counts and column semantics (lines 29-55) — no source-tier check, no evidence-file precondition. Nothing in `harness/` writes results-evidence files; they are hand-authored. `harness/parse_box_dump.py` (added post-hoc in de87ba3) writes a source sha256 but is wired into no ingest path. So the finding's recommendation is genuinely unimplemented, not a duplicate of an existing control.

## Corrections to the finding (do not change the verdict)

1. **Minor wording imprecision.** "versus 8/7 where every game carried one" is true of the *evidence JSON* (all 15 games have `source_note`), not of the CSV `source` cell — the 8/7 CSV rows are equally generic: `websearch_multi_source(gamePk-keyed where available)`. The sentence reads as if the 8/7 CSV cells were richer. They were not; the difference is the existence of the sidecar file.

2. **The 8/7 baseline is weaker than implied, which strengthens the argument.** Of 15 games in the 8/7 evidence file, **7 carry only a single source id** despite the file's `provenance_class` asserting `WEBSEARCH_MULTI_SOURCE` — NYM@PIT, LAA@MIA, HOU@SD, TB@SEA, CLE@CWS, COL@STL, ATH@BOS. Three of the four games that went wrong on 8/8 (LAA@MIA, TB@SEA, ATH@BOS) were among those single-sourced 8/7 rows. So the "multi_source" label was already an unaudited day-level assertion on the best-documented day; 8/8 removed even the ability to check it.

3. **The recommendation needs two fixes to be implementable.** (a) The path is wrong — the convention is `data/mlb/evidence/websearch/<DATE>_finals.json`, and a blanket "evidence file must exist" rule would wrongly block the higher-tier `owner_board_paste` (8/6) and `owner_box_dump(tier1)` ingests, which have *better* provenance. The precondition must be tier-aware: every row needs a provenance record of *some* declared tier, hashed. (b) **A novelty-only echo check is necessary but not sufficient.** Three of the four wrong 8/8 games carried no real id at all — synthetic keys `ws0808-LAAMIA`, `ws0808-DETSF`, `ws0808-TBSEA` (TB@SEA even *lost* the gamePk 823103 it had on 8/7). The fourth, ATH@BOS, carried gamePk 824726 — one *below* 8/7's 824727. Across the slate the 8/8 gamePks move down for 5 matchups and up for 2 relative to 8/7, which is the signature of ids derived by arithmetic rather than looked up. A "has this id appeared before" rule passes a fabricated-but-novel id. The guard must check id *validity* (resolvable, date-consistent) as well as novelty, and must reject synthetic `ws<date>-<matchup>` keys as a source identifier at all.

Relevant paths: `/home/user/sports-model/data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv`, `/home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-07_finals.json`, `/home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/2026-08-10_results_correction.json`, `/home/user/sports-model/data/wnba/evidence_2026-08-08_finals.json`, `/home/user/sports-model/harness/healthcheck.py`, `/home/user/sports-model/harness/parse_box_dump.py`.

adversarial_verifications.title: CONFIRMED: ATH@BOS orientation flip is real, self-consistent, and undetectable by every existing repo check (two claims in the write-up are overstated)
adversarial_verifications.reasoning:
CONFIRMED. Every checkable claim holds, and I reproduced the failure mechanically.

**1. The row is exactly as quoted.** `git show 6e436db:/home/user/sports-model/data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv` contains:
`mlb,2026,mlb:2026:824726,2026-08-08,final,ATH,BOS,3,7,1,4,10,0,Fenway Park,,,,,,websearch_multi_source(ESPN/MLB.com) 2026-08-09,2026-08-09T05:42:19Z`
Authoritative is ATH 7, BOS 3 (/home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/2026-08-10_results_correction.json, `winner_flipped: true`, `linescore_verified: true`). Same two digits, opposite sides.

**2. Derived fields really were computed from the flipped pair.** margin 4 = 7−3 ✓, total 10 ✓, home_win 1 ✓. Critically, **total is invariant under an orientation flip** (10 either way) and only home_win and the sign of margin change — so a total cross-check is structurally powerless here, and the `ml_asof` rebuild recomputes `label_total`/`label_margin`/`home_win` from the same pair, so it reconciles with itself.

**3. Not an echo — and that distinguishes it from the other three errors.** 8/7 ATH@BOS was 1-13 (results.csv + /home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-07_finals.json). By contrast the 8/8 rows for DET@SF (2-5) and TB@SEA (2-1) are verbatim copies of their 8/7 finals, and LAA@MIA 4-3 is near the 8/7 4-2. So ATH@BOS is a separate error class, as the finding says.

**4. Invisible to every internal check the repo has — verified, not assumed.** healthcheck.py:34-41 is the only results.csv gate: finals count ≥1505, no duplicate game_ids, `home_win` in {0,1} and `total` non-empty, freshness ≤2d. Nothing binds a team name to a score. A repo-wide grep shows **no `winner` field exists in any results artifact** — the only hit is `FORBIDDEN_RESULT_KEYS` in forecast_registry.py:51 (scoped to forecast payloads via `_payload_result_keys`, so the recommended field is not blocked there). And commit 6e436db added **no MLB evidence file for 8/8** at all (only `data/wnba/evidence_2026-08-08_finals.json`), so nothing independent of the CSV row ever recorded who won.

**5. Impact on the biggest favourite is real.** In /home/user/sports-model/cards/2026-08-08_card.json, ATH@BOS `mkt_home_prob` 0.702 is the slate maximum (next 0.610; ml_home −250). V13 also had BOS at `home_wp` 0.614. So the flip gifted a win to the market's single most confident side *and* to the model. Recomputing the grading from the card: the wrong results reproduce the prior session's reported V13 7/15 and market 6/15 exactly; the authoritative results give V13 8/15 and market 7/15.

**Impact the finding understates:** build_ml_asof.py:203-206 folds each final into cumulative team run-for/run-against (`rf[a]+=asc; ra[a]+=hsc`), so the flip also credits ATH with 3 scored / 7 allowed and BOS with 7/3 in the ML feature stream — contamination beyond the grading, invisible for the same reason.

**Two overstatements worth correcting (they do not change the verdict):**
- The title's "no consistency check *can* catch" is false as a universal; the accurate version is the impact paragraph's "invisible to every internal check the repo has." I ran the historical error shape through harness/parse_box_dump.py: with a linescore present, `3 @ 7` against away-first innings rows is caught — `linescore_ok=False`, validate fails with "linescore does not sum to the stated final 3-7."
- The recommendation's claim that the linescore check "independently binds each score to its own team's innings" is not accurate. `_linescore_check` takes the **first two linescore-shaped rows after the score line, positionally** — they are never team-labeled. I confirmed two residual holes: a whole-block reversal (team names, scores and linescore rows all flipped together) parses as `BOS 3 @ 7 ATH` with `linescore_ok=True` and validate PASS; and a block with no linescore parses `ATH 3 @ 7 BOS` with `linescore_ok=None` and validate PASS — which matters because the correction record itself states 3 of 30 games in the tier-1 dump had no linescore. So the winner-name assertion is doing the real work; the linescore check is a useful but weaker partner than described.

**Root-cause caveat:** "orientation flip" is the best inference, not a proof, because no 8/8 MLB evidence file was ever written — there is no captured snippet showing what the ingesting model read. The digit permutation, plus the fact that the other three errors are 8/7 echoes/reconstructions, makes it the strongest explanation, and /home/user/sports-model/docs/audits/2026-08-10_lesser_model_workflow_audit.json reaches the same conclusion. The impact claim does not depend on the mechanism: however `3,7` got written, the row is self-consistent and no existing check would have flagged it.

adversarial_verifications.title: LAA@MIA 4-3 "anchored reconstruction" — row defect real, but impact claim inverted and mechanism unproven
adversarial_verifications.reasoning:
## What I verified

**The data defect is real (git-confirmed).** Commit `6e436db` wrote `mlb,2026,mlb:2026:ws0808-LAAMIA,2026-08-08,final,LAA,MIA,4,3,0,-1,7,0,loanDepot park,...,websearch_multi_source(ESPN/MLB.com) 2026-08-09` to `/home/user/sports-model/data/backfill/mlb/2026/results.csv`; commit `de87ba3` corrected it to `0,7,1,7,7`. The 8/7 anchor is exactly as quoted: `/home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/evidence/websearch/2026-08-07_finals.json` has LAA 4 @ MIA 2 with `"gamePk": null, "source_note": "foxsports boxscore 96406 (LAA 4-2)"` — a single tier-3 source. And 4-3 matches no LAA@MIA row anywhere in the repo (8/7 = 4-2 tier-3; 8/8 = 0-7 tier-1; 8/9 = 3-12 tier-1). That much of the evidence paragraph checks out line by line.

## Where the finding breaks: the impact claim is inverted

The finding says the bad row "flipped a game the market had at MIA 59.4% into a 'winning dog' — one of the three legs of the 'compression caught winning dogs' conclusion." Both halves are false.

1. **LAA is not one of the three legs.** `/home/user/sports-model/data/mlb/forecasts/2026-08-08_grading.json` names them explicitly: "compression toward .500 caught winning dogs (WSH/CWS/TB)". The Pass-2 legs are MIL/CWS/TB. LAA appears in neither list.

2. **The error cost V13 a hit; it did not manufacture one.** `/home/user/sports-model/cards/2026-08-08_card.json` row NC02 has `v13.home_wp = 0.526` and `mkt_home_prob = 0.594` — V13 and the market **both picked MIA**. Under the bogus LAA 4-3 both were wrong; under the truth (MIA 7-0) both are right. I re-graded all 15 games off the card by hand and reproduced the reported 7/15 and 6/15 exactly, then re-graded against the authoritative results and got 8/15 and 7/15 — matching `2026-08-08_grading_CORRECTED.json` (V13 7→8, market 6→7, margin unchanged at +1). The bad row's actual effect was to *inflate* the "upset-heavy night" framing (market 6/15 rather than 7/15) and *depress* V13's headline accuracy. The finding asserts the opposite sign.

## Where the finding is unproven: "anchored reconstruction" as a distinct failure mode

The mechanism claim rests entirely on the 8/7 home score being 2 — which comes from a single-source, no-gamePk, tier-3 record, i.e. exactly the record class this finding argues cannot be trusted. It uses an untrusted number to establish a novel taxonomy.

And the simpler explanation is right there in the sibling errors. Comparing 8/7 → ingested 8/8 → authoritative 8/8:
- DET@SF: 2-5 → **2-5** → 8-0 (exact carry-forward of yesterday)
- TB@SEA: 2-1 → **2-1** → 3-2 (exact carry-forward of yesterday)
- LAA@MIA: 4-2 → 4-3 → 0-7 (off by one in the home score)
- ATH@BOS: 1-13 → 3-7 → 7-3 (not carry-forward; the true pair with sides transposed)

Two of the four are *exact* prior-day carry-forwards. That makes plain carry-forward the parsimonious explanation for LAA@MIA too, with the tier-3 8/7 row being the thing that is off by one — in which case it is a duplicate after all and the "defeats duplicate alarms" argument collapses. The repo cannot settle this: the only tier-1 data is 8/8 and 8/9.

Supporting signal the audit missed: all three carry-forward-contaminated matchups (LAAMIA, DETSF, TBSEA) are precisely the 8/8 rows written with synthetic `ws0808-*` ids and no gamePk. 3 of the 8 no-gamePk rows are prior-day contaminated; 0 of the 7 gamePk-keyed rows are (the one gamePk-keyed error, ATH@BOS `824726`, is a transposition, a different mechanism).

## Where the differential-danger argument is hypothetical

"It is not a duplicate of yesterday, so a duplicate-score alarm misses it" presumes a control that does not exist. `/home/user/sports-model/harness/healthcheck.py:35` is the only duplicate check in the harness — `check("no duplicate game_ids", len(ids)==len(set(ids)))` — it compares ids, never scores. The two *exact* carry-forwards sailed through it unflagged. All four errors defeated every existing check equally; LAA@MIA is not uniquely evasive relative to the real control set.

## Where the recommendation stands up

The control gap is genuine. `results.csv` has 21 columns (`sport,season,game_id,date,status,away,home,away_score,home_score,home_win,margin,total,neutral_site,venue,close_ml_away,close_ml_home,close_spread_home,close_total,features_json,source,ingested_utc`) — no tier field. `RESULT_SOURCE_TIER` appears nowhere in the repo except the docstring at `/home/user/sports-model/harness/parse_box_dump.py:16-19` that points at it as if it existed in "the results schema". Provenance is free-text prose in `source`, and no check reads that column. So "tier discipline is documented, not enforced" is correct — though the sibling audit items at `/home/user/sports-model/docs/audits/2026-08-10_lesser_model_workflow_audit.json:172-174` already make this same recommendation with better-grounded evidence.

## Verdict

PARTIAL. The underlying row was wrong and was used to grade — but that is already documented and corrected in the repo. What this finding adds on top of the known correction is a mechanism claim it cannot support and an impact claim that is backwards. The stated HIGH severity rides on the impact paragraph; with that paragraph falsified, the incremental severity is LOW. The more actionable version of the same thesis is the one the finding under-sells: a same-matchup-consecutive-day score-equality check would have caught 2 of the 4 errors on 8/8 outright, at essentially zero cost, and no such check exists.
